section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what age can a Nevada teen apply for a learner's permit?
options: a:14 and a half,b:15,c:15 and a half,d:16
note: Nevada allows teens to apply for a learner's permit at age 15½ (15 years and 6 months). The learner's permit requires a parent or guardian's consent and allows supervised driving practice under Nevada's GDL program.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for a driver age 21 or older in Nevada?
note: Nevada sets the per se DUI limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. Reaching 0.08% BAC alone is sufficient for a DUI conviction regardless of apparent impairment. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Extreme desert heat in Nevada can cause which tire hazard that drivers should be aware of?
options: a:Tires become sticky and slow the vehicle,b:Tires can over-inflate and potentially blow out due to heat expansion,c:Tires deflate rapidly in hot weather,d:Tires provide more traction in extreme heat
note: Nevada's desert heat causes the air inside tires to expand, which increases tire pressure. An already over-inflated tire can blow out suddenly in extreme heat. Check tire pressure when tires are cold, and follow the vehicle manufacturer's recommended PSI — not the maximum printed on the tire sidewall.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in Las Vegas and see a pedestrian crossing in a marked crosswalk. What must you do?
options: a:Honk to alert the pedestrian and proceed carefully,b:Slow to 15 mph and pass behind the pedestrian,c:Stop and yield the right of way until the pedestrian has fully crossed your lane,d:Yield only if the pedestrian is directly in your path
note: Nevada law requires drivers to stop and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. Las Vegas has extremely heavy pedestrian traffic, especially near the Strip and casino areas. You must remain stopped until the pedestrian has fully cleared your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit in a Nevada urban area when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:20 mph,b:25 mph,c:30 mph,d:35 mph
note: Nevada's default speed limit in urban and residential areas is 25 mph when no other limit is posted. In school zones and near playgrounds, the limit is typically 15 mph when children are present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Nevada highway when a dust storm suddenly reduces visibility to near zero. What should you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and pull onto the shoulder to wait it out with feet on the brakes,b:Speed up to exit the dust storm quickly,c:Pull completely off the road, turn off your lights, and wait until the storm passes,d:Continue at reduced speed using your high beams
note: In a severe Nevada dust storm (haboob), pull completely off the paved road surface, turn off your headlights (so other drivers don't follow them into a stopped vehicle), put the car in park, and keep your foot off the brake pedal. Wait until the storm passes before continuing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Nevada's zero tolerance law sets the illegal BAC for drivers under 21 at:
options: a:0.00% — any detectable amount,b:0.02%,c:0.04%,d:0.08%
note: Nevada's zero tolerance law sets the underage DUI threshold at 0.02% BAC for drivers under 21. Any amount at or above 0.02% results in license suspension and other penalties. This is lower than the adult limit of 0.08%.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to make a right turn at a red light in Nevada. What must you do?
options: a:Proceed without stopping if no traffic is visible,b:Stop completely, yield to pedestrians and cross traffic, then turn if no sign prohibits it,c:Right turns on red are prohibited statewide in Nevada,d:Signal and proceed — right turns on red have the right of way
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Nevada after a complete stop and yielding to all pedestrians and cross traffic. Always check for 'No Turn on Red' signs, which are common near the Las Vegas Strip and at high-pedestrian intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does Nevada's Move Over law require when passing a stopped emergency vehicle on a multi-lane highway?
options: a:Slow to 15 mph regardless of lane position,b:Move one lane away from the stopped vehicle if safely possible, or slow to a safe speed,c:Stop completely on the shoulder,d:Move over only for law enforcement, not for tow trucks
note: Nevada's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from any stopped emergency, law enforcement, or roadside assistance vehicle with active warning lights. If a lane change is not safely possible, slow to a reasonable speed below the posted limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Nevada, it is illegal to use a handheld cell phone while driving. What is the penalty for a first offense?
options: a:A verbal warning with no fine,b:A fine but no points added to your license,c:A fine and demerit points added to your driving record,d:License suspension for 30 days
note: Nevada's distracted driving law prohibits handheld cell phone use while driving. A first offense results in a fine AND demerit points added to your driving record. Hands-free devices are permitted. Repeat offenses carry higher fines and more demerit points.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Nevada highway and the road surface appears wet and shiny despite no recent rain. This may indicate:
options: a:The road was recently sealed and is still wet,b:Black ice — a nearly invisible layer of ice on the road surface,c:Fresh paint markings on the road,d:An optical illusion — the road is dry
note: A wet, shiny road surface in cold weather with no recent rain can indicate black ice — a thin, nearly transparent layer of ice that is extremely dangerous. Black ice forms when temperatures drop and moisture freezes on the road. Slow down immediately and avoid sudden steering or braking inputs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a school bus stopped with flashing red lights on a Nevada highway, what must ALL traffic do on an undivided road?
options: a:Traffic behind the bus must stop; traffic in front may proceed,b:All traffic in both directions must stop at least 15 feet from the bus,c:Slow to 15 mph and pass carefully,d:Stop only if children are visibly exiting
note: In Nevada, on an undivided road, all traffic in both directions must stop at least 15 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm. Wait until the lights stop and the arm retracts. On a divided highway with a physical median, only traffic behind the bus must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a Nevada freeway with multiple lanes in each direction, which lane should you use for normal travel?
options: a:The far left (fast) lane at all times for maximum speed,b:The right lanes for normal driving; left lanes for passing only,c:The center lane regardless of speed,d:Any lane — Nevada has no lane use rules
note: Nevada law requires slower vehicles to stay in the right lanes. The left lane on multi-lane freeways is designated for passing — not for sustained travel at the speed limit. Move right after completing a pass. This is especially important on Las Vegas freeways where traffic merges frequently.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum following distance recommended in Nevada under normal highway driving conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Nevada recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. On Nevada's desert highways, consider increasing to 4 seconds — the roads are long and straight, making it tempting to tailgate, but stopping distances at high speeds remain significant.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must use your headlights in Nevada:
options: a:Only between midnight and 5 AM,b:From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and when visibility is reduced,c:Only when driving outside of city limits,d:Only when other drivers have their headlights on
note: Nevada requires headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise and whenever weather or smoke reduces visibility. Using headlights also makes your vehicle more visible to others — turn them on whenever there is doubt.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking on a Nevada street, how far may your vehicle be from the curb?
options: a:6 inches,b:12 inches,c:18 inches,d:24 inches
note: Nevada requires parallel-parked vehicles to be within 18 inches of the curb. Parking further out can obstruct traffic flow and create a hazard. Use your mirrors and take your time to position the vehicle properly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Nevada, what is required before passing a vehicle on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Signal for at least 5 seconds before moving into the oncoming lane,b:Ensure there is a broken yellow centerline on your side, adequate distance, and no oncoming traffic,c:Honk to alert the driver ahead that you are passing,d:Pass on the right shoulder if it is paved
note: Before passing on a two-lane Nevada highway, you must confirm: (1) there is a broken yellow center line on your side, (2) you have a clear view of at least 1/3 mile ahead, (3) no oncoming traffic is close, and (4) you have enough speed and distance to complete the pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does it mean when a traffic signal shows a steady yellow light?
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection before the light turns red,b:The light is about to turn green — prepare to go,c:The light is about to turn red — slow down and stop if safe to do so,d:Yield to cross traffic and then proceed
note: A steady yellow signal in Nevada means the light is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so. Only proceed if you are so close to the intersection that stopping would be unsafe. Never speed up to 'beat' a yellow light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do if your vehicle's brakes fail while driving in Nevada?
options: a:Turn off the ignition to slow the engine,b:Pump the brakes rapidly to build pressure, downshift, use the parking brake gently, and look for an escape route,c:Turn the wheel sharply to generate friction,d:Immediately open your door to create wind resistance
note: If your brakes fail, rapidly pump the brake pedal to try to build hydraulic pressure, downshift to use engine braking, gently apply the parking brake, and steer toward an escape route such as an uphill slope or soft shoulder. Never turn off the ignition while moving as it can lock the steering wheel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on a Nevada interstate and a vehicle is merging from an on-ramp, what should through traffic do?
options: a:Maintain speed — merging vehicles must yield,b:Move to the left lane if possible to give the merging vehicle room,c:Slow to 25 mph and let the merging vehicle enter,d:Flash your headlights to warn the merging driver
note: When safe, Nevada drivers should move left to allow merging vehicles space to enter the freeway. While the merging driver is responsible for matching highway speed and finding a gap, courteous drivers facilitate smooth merging. If moving left is not possible, maintaining steady speed helps merging drivers predict your position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit on most Nevada interstates for passenger vehicles?
options: a:65 mph,b:70 mph,c:75 mph,d:80 mph
note: Most Nevada interstate highways have a speed limit of 75 mph for passenger vehicles in rural areas. Some sections near Las Vegas and Reno have lower limits of 65 mph. Always check posted signs — exceeding the limit on Nevada's open desert highways is a common and costly mistake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Nevada, can you use your horn whenever you feel like it?
options: a:Yes — horns are for any communication purpose,b:No — horns should only be used to warn other drivers of a hazard or to avoid a collision,c:Yes, as long as it is not between 10 PM and 7 AM,d:Only when another driver is at fault
note: Nevada's vehicle code specifies that horns are for safety use only — to warn of a hazard or to prevent a collision. Using your horn for non-safety reasons (expressing frustration, greeting friends) is prohibited, though enforcement is rare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the primary danger of driving in heavy Las Vegas traffic after a light rain?
options: a:Sand washed onto the road from the desert reduces traction,b:Light rain mixes with oil on the road surface, making it extremely slippery,c:Sudden flooding always occurs after any rain in Las Vegas,d:Visibility improves dramatically after rain
note: After a dry period, rain mixes with accumulated oil and grease on Nevada road surfaces, creating a very slippery film. This 'first rain' hazard is especially dangerous in urban areas like Las Vegas where vehicles deposit oil over time. Reduce speed and increase following distance during and after light rain.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid white line between lanes of traffic traveling in the same direction means:
options: a:Lane changes are prohibited,b:Lane changes are discouraged but permitted if necessary,c:The lane to your right is an exit lane,d:The lane is closing ahead
note: A solid white line between lanes indicates that lane changes are prohibited at that point. This is commonly used near intersections, at highway entrances and exits, and in construction zones. A broken white line means lane changes are permitted when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are approaching a four-way stop at the same time as three other drivers. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The largest vehicle always goes first,b:The driver who arrived first goes first; ties are resolved by yielding to the right,c:All drivers must wait for a signal from a police officer,d:The driver going straight always has the right of way
note: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive goes first. When two or more vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the driver on your right. If all vehicles arrive at exactly the same time, the driver going straight has priority over those turning.

question: Who is required to wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle in Nevada?
options: a:Only those in the front seats.,b:Only adult passengers.,c:All occupants of the vehicle.,d:Only the driver.
note: Nevada law requires every person in a moving vehicle to use a seat belt or an approved child restraint, regardless of seating position. Children must be in proper child safety seats or booster seats as required by age, weight, and height, and adults and older children must use seat belts in both front and rear seats.

question: Where are stop lines painted?
options: a:Next to churches and schools.,b:In curves and on hills.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across the lane at intersections and before crosswalks to show where you must stop your vehicle. You must stop with your front bumper behind the stop line so pedestrians and cross traffic have a clear and safe space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle coming from the right has the right-of-way.,b:The vehicle coming from the left has the right-of-way.,c:Whoever honks first
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), you must yield to a vehicle that arrives from your right. This rule helps prevent confusion when vehicles arrive at about the same time.

question: What best ensures safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.,b:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.,c:Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.
note: The safest way to back up is to check behind the vehicle before you get in, looking for children, pedestrians, and obstacles. Mirrors alone can miss low or close objects, so a walk-around check greatly reduces blind spots.

question: May you drive around or under a lowering railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never drive around or under a lowering gate.,b:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,c:If you first look carefully in both directions.
note: You must never drive around or under a lowering or lowered railroad gate. Always wait until the lights and bells stop and the gate is fully raised before crossing, even if you do not see a train.

question: What device is often used on highways to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?
options: a:White lines on the side of the road.,b:Arrows painted or displayed to show turning lanes.,c:Flashing red lights.
note: Arrows painted on the pavement or shown on overhead signs tell you which lanes are for turning and which are for going straight. Follow these arrows to be in the correct lane before you reach the intersection.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road mean?
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and no passing is allowed.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and no passing is allowed.
note: A double solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross it only for limited reasons like turning left into a driveway or side road when it is safe.

question: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, when should you proceed?
options: a:Go through as soon as the train passes.,b:Wait to proceed until you have a clear view of all tracks.,c:Stop on the first railroad track and watch for another train.
note: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, a second train can come from either direction on another track. After one train passes, wait until the gates are fully raised (if present) and you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions before proceeding. Never stop on the tracks; always make sure there is enough space on the far side to clear all tracks completely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A solid yellow light
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, watching carefully for cross traffic or hazards and being prepared to stop if needed. A flashing red light means stop completely, then proceed when it is safe, like a stop sign. A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red and you should stop if you can do so safely.

question: After an upsetting incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home,b:Drive fast to blow off steam,c:Play loud music to distract yourself
note: Strong emotions like anger, frustration, or sadness can distract you, slow your reactions, and lead to risky decisions. If you are upset, take time to calm down before driving—sit quietly, take deep breaths, or walk for a few minutes. Do not try to “blow off steam” by speeding or distracting yourself with loud music, because that keeps your focus off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering a street from a garage or alley.,b:When drivers are on a road to your right and you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.,c:When your traffic signal shows a green arrow but pedestrians or vehicles are still in the intersection.
note: You must always yield to traffic and pedestrians when entering a street from a driveway, alley, or garage because you are joining a road where others already have the right‑of‑way. At an unmarked intersection, you yield to vehicles on your right, not your left. A green arrow gives you the right‑of‑way for that movement, but you still must yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection or still clearing it.

question: When the road may be slippery, what is the safest action?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,b:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.,c:Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: On wet, icy, or otherwise slippery roads, tires have less grip, so it takes longer to stop and is easier to lose control. Reduce your speed, increase your following distance, and make all steering, braking, and accelerating movements gently. Avoid using cruise control on slippery surfaces so you can respond quickly to changes in traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do several seconds before making a turn?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Turn the wheel.,c:Use your signal.
note: Use your turn signal several seconds (about three to four seconds, or at least 100 feet at low speeds and 300 feet on highways in many states) before turning so other drivers and pedestrians have time to see your intention and react safely.

question: What is the key principle for speed management when driving through curves?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve,b:Enter at the posted speed and then slow in the curve,c:Accelerate before entering the curve
note: Slow down before you enter a curve, then maintain a safe, steady speed through it. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause loss of traction and control because your tires are already working to change direction.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It causes hearing loss.,b:It increases pollution only.,c:It can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment causing poisoning.
note: A leaky exhaust can let carbon monoxide and other poisonous gases enter the passenger compartment. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless and can quickly cause sickness, unconsciousness, or death, so exhaust leaks must be repaired immediately.

question: If a road is covered with water, you should:
options: a:Turn around and find another route,b:Drive through carefully at low speed,c:Drive until water reaches the hubcaps
note: If a road is flooded, turn around and find another route. You cannot reliably judge water depth or the strength of the current, and even shallow moving water can sweep a vehicle away or hide road damage.

question: True or False: Cars begin to lose traction and can hydroplane at speeds of 70 mph.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Hydroplaning can begin at much lower speeds than 70 mph—often around 35 mph—if there is enough water on the road and your tires are worn or underinflated. Reduce speed in wet conditions to maintain traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down and carefully continue through.,b:Stop fully, then proceed when the way is clear.,c:Stop and wait for a flashing green light.,d:Treat it like a yield sign and merge cautiously.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb required?
options: a:Is necessary only during the maneuver, not before.,b:Is a good driving habit and is required by law.,c:Is necessary only if other traffic is present.
note: Turn signals are required by law before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb. You must signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet—so other road users have time to see and react to your intentions.

question: Which best describes defensive driving?
options: a:Driving aggressively to assert right-of-way.,b:Using safe strategies to avoid crashes by adjusting to conditions.,c:Driving faster than others to reduce exposure time.,d:Avoiding using signals to prevent confusion.
note: Defensive driving means staying alert, anticipating potential hazards, and adjusting your speed and position for traffic, road, and weather conditions so you can avoid collisions before they happen.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, you should:
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can clear it completely,b:Move forward as far as possible to get closer to the front car,c:Go slowly until traffic ahead moves
note: You should not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through it without stopping. Entering when traffic is stopped ahead can leave you blocking the intersection, which is unsafe and often illegal.

question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Try to get out of their way and avoid eye contact.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass to teach them a lesson.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Challenge them by braking suddenly.
note: If another driver is aggressive, stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and safely let them pass when you can. Do not speed up, brake suddenly, or engage with them, as this can escalate the situation.

question: A steady yellow traffic light means:
options: a:Stop immediately even if in the intersection,b:Speed up to clear the intersection,c:Slow down and prepare to stop because the light is about to turn red
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through with caution.

question: What affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
options: a:The time of day.,b:Signal lights.,c:Road and pavement conditions.,d:The color of nearby vehicles.
note: Road and pavement conditions strongly affect how quickly you can stop. Wet, icy, gravel, or damaged pavement reduces traction and increases stopping distance, so you must slow down and allow more space to stop safely.

question: What is a common cause of many crashes?
options: a:Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.,b:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.,c:Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a major cause of crashes. Even if you are at or below the posted speed limit, you must slow down when roads are wet, icy, congested, or visibility is poor so you can stop or react in time.

question: You may not parallel park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
options: a:15 feet,b:20 feet,c:30 feet
note: You must not park too close to a fire hydrant so firefighters can access it quickly in an emergency. In many states, including Nevada, you may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the left side mirror.,b:Quickly glance over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,c:Look into the rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show areas directly alongside your vehicle, called blind spots. Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: If two railroad tracks are side by side, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.,b:You must always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Look for a second train on the other track before crossing.
note: At crossings with more than one track, a second train can approach on another track, sometimes hidden by the first train. After one train passes, wait until you have a clear view of all tracks in both directions and are sure no other trains are coming before you proceed.

question: Road surfaces become especially slippery when?
options: a:During the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm,b:After it has been raining for several hours,c:The day after it rains
note: When rain first begins, oil and residue on the road surface mix with the water and rise to the top, making the pavement very slick for the first several minutes. As rain continues, much of this washes away and traction generally improves, though you must still drive carefully.

question: True or false: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only at night,d:Only when other vehicles are present
note: You must signal any time you move your vehicle from the curb into traffic so that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know your intention. Signaling before leaving the curb helps prevent collisions with vehicles already in the lane you are entering.

question: A curb painted which color indicates a loading zone or other parking restriction?
options: a:Yellow,b:Blue,c:White
note: A yellow curb usually marks a loading zone or other limited-time parking area. You may be allowed to stop only long enough to load or unload passengers or freight, and local signs or rules will specify the exact restrictions.

question: An octagonal road sign always indicates which instruction?
options: a:Hospital,b:Speed limit,c:Stop
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign is reserved exclusively for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Which item does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much alcohol you drink.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,d:How much time passes between drinks.
note: Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) is mainly affected by how much alcohol you consume, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, and how much time passes while your body metabolizes the alcohol. The type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, or liquor) does not change the BAC produced by a given amount of pure alcohol; what matters is the total amount of alcohol you take in and the rate at which you drink it.

question: Hydroplaning is most commonly caused by:
options: a:Too much speed on wet roads causing tires to ride on water,b:Sudden stops,c:Worn windshield wipers
note: At higher speeds on wet pavement, tires can lose contact with the road and ride on a film of water, causing loss of steering control (hydroplaning).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers respond to a steady yellow arrow signal?
options: a:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,c:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected signal is ending; stop if you can do so safely unless already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is correct?
options: a:Speeding is safe if you are an experienced driver.,b:Speed has no effect on crash severity.,c:Driving faster always increases fuel efficiency.,d:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
note: Both excessive speed and driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous. Higher speeds increase the chance of fatalities in crashes.

question: What color are highway guide signs that show directions and mileages?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Guide (destination) signs are green and provide directional and mileage information to drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signal?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,d:All of the above.
note: Turn signals must be used any time you change your vehicle’s direction or move laterally in traffic. This includes changing lanes, entering or leaving parking spaces, and pulling into traffic from alleys or parking areas so other drivers and pedestrians can anticipate your movement.

question: If a vehicle starts to hydroplane (skid on water), should the driver immediately apply the brakes?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: When a vehicle hydroplanes, the tires lose contact with the road and ride on a thin layer of water. You should ease off the accelerator and steer gently in the direction you want to go. Do not slam on the brakes, because hard braking can cause a complete loss of control and make the skid worse.

question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A single broken yellow line means traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed in either direction when it is safe and legal. You must still check for oncoming traffic, ensure you have enough clear distance, and obey any additional signs or markings that may restrict passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from multilane one-way streets, you should begin your turn from which lane?
options: a:The left lane,b:The right lane,c:The center of the intersection
note: On a one‑way street with multiple lanes, you normally begin a left turn from the lane closest to the left curb or edge of the roadway. This positions you correctly for entering the proper lane on the new street and reduces conflicts with other traffic, unless signs or lane markings direct you otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:Once you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road, just before the exit lane.,c:Once you see a toll booth.
note: You should maintain highway speed until you are safely in the exit (deceleration) lane, then slow down to the posted exit or ramp speed. Braking on the main travel lanes can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: When you approach a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Speed up to get past the hazard,b:Stop and wait for a green light,c:Slow down and proceed with caution
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution, not stop. You should slow down, scan the intersection or area carefully, and continue only when it is safe. Be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles.

question: How far ahead should drivers look when traveling on a freeway?
options: a:10 to 15 seconds,b:20 to 30 seconds,c:15 seconds
note: On freeways and other high‑speed roads, drivers are generally taught to look about 10–15 seconds ahead so they can see hazards early and adjust smoothly. Looking this far ahead helps you avoid sudden braking and last‑second lane changes.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a collision, what should you do?
options: a:Not move your vehicle under any circumstances.,b:Wait until the police arrive before moving your vehicle.,c:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway, if possible.
note: If you are in a minor collision and your vehicle can be driven, you should move it out of the travel lanes to the shoulder or a safe location. This helps prevent additional crashes. You must stay at the scene and exchange information with the other parties involved.

question: What do round traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Upcoming railroad crossings.
note: Round traffic signs are used specifically for advance warning of railroad crossings. When you see a round railroad warning sign, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: Which driving habit can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Slowing down gradually to avoid unnecessary stops,b:Accelerating quickly then coasting,c:Idling in your driveway with the engine running
note: To save fuel, look ahead and slow down gradually instead of making sudden stops. Smooth, steady driving with gentle acceleration and braking uses less gasoline than rapid starts, hard braking, or unnecessary idling.

question: If you are in the left lane and want to move right, what should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for vehicles in the blind spot,b:Look over your left shoulder only,c:Signal and change lanes without checking mirrors
note: Before changing lanes to the right, check your mirrors, signal your intention, and then quickly look over your right shoulder to check your blind spot. This ensures there is no vehicle in the area your mirrors cannot see before you move into the lane.

question: What is a 'No zone'?
options: a:A designated no passing zone,b:A one-way traffic area,c:The blind spot of a large vehicle
note: A 'No Zone' is the large blind spot around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you drive in these areas, the truck or bus driver may not know you are there, so you should avoid lingering in these zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in a line at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after the vehicles ahead pass, what should you do?
options: a:Bring your vehicle to a complete stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,b:Proceed through without stopping again.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign because the way is clear.,d:Honk to warn any unseen traffic before proceeding.
note: At a stop sign, each driver must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, even if vehicles ahead have already stopped and gone. After stopping, proceed only when it is your turn and the way is clear.

question: When parallel parking, how close should your wheels be to the curb?
options: a:10 inches,b:12 inches,c:18 inches
note: When parallel parking, position your vehicle so your wheels are within 18 inches of the curb and do not block traffic visibility.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, how should you return to the road?
options: a:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,b:Slow down, regain control, and carefully steer back onto the pavement.,c:Stop on the shoulder and re-enter quickly.,d:Accelerate and yank the wheel to return.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually without jerking the wheel or braking hard. Once you have control and your speed is reduced, gently steer back onto the pavement when there is a safe gap in traffic.

question: When making an emergency roadside stop, is it necessary to set the parking brake?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When you stop on the roadside, you should secure the vehicle so it cannot roll. Setting the parking brake, placing the vehicle in park (or in gear for a manual), and turning on hazard lights help prevent movement and make your vehicle more visible to other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians.,b:Stop and look for nearby police cars.,c:Maintain your normal driving speed.
note: A green light allows you to proceed, but it does not give you the right to endanger others. When turning right on green, you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any traffic already in the intersection before completing your turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where are U-turns prohibited?
options: a:On a hill with less than 500 feet visibility, in curves, or where posted prohibitions exist,b:Anywhere in a city,c:Only on highways with center barriers
note: U‑turns are illegal where you cannot see far enough ahead, such as on hills or curves with limited visibility, or where signs or road markings prohibit them. Even where they are allowed, you may only make a U‑turn when it can be done safely without interfering with other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal displays a steady green arrow, what does it permit?
options: a:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,c:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.
note: A steady green arrow gives you a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, meaning oncoming traffic is stopped or otherwise controlled. You may turn, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Driving well under the posted speed limit is generally:
options: a:Always safe,b:Recommended at all times,c:Potentially dangerous and can force others to take risks
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be hazardous because it causes other drivers to brake or change lanes unexpectedly and may encourage risky passing. You should drive at a speed that is safe for conditions while not unnecessarily obstructing traffic.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign usually indicates what?
options: a:A warning about potential hazards or changes in road conditions,b:A school zone,c:A recreational area
note: Diamond-shaped signs are general warning signs. They alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or pedestrian crossings. They are usually yellow, or orange in work zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,b:Keep your speed and ignore the backup.,c:Speed up suddenly to clear the way.,d:Turn on hazard lights and continue slowly.
note: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up, you are creating a hazard. When it is safe, pull off to the right side of the road or into a turnout area and let the backed‑up traffic pass, then re-enter when clear.

question: When is parking or stopping on a freeway shoulder permitted?
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,b:As long as you turn on your four-way (emergency) flashers.,c:Only in an emergency.
note: Stopping or parking on a freeway shoulder is generally illegal except for emergencies, such as a breakdown, flat tire, or medical problem. In an emergency, pull as far onto the shoulder as possible, turn on your hazard lights, and seek help.

question: How does increasing your vehicle’s speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It decreases your field of vision.,c:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision effectively narrows. You see less to the sides and may miss hazards such as pedestrians, cyclists, or cross traffic. Slowing down widens your field of vision and improves your ability to spot dangers.

question: Which is true about driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Roads are most slippery just after rain begins.,b:Hydroplaning can occur on wet roads.,c:You should allow additional stopping distance.,d:All of the above.
note: On wet pavement, roads are often most slippery just after the rain begins because oil and dirt rise to the surface. Water on the road can cause hydroplaning, where your tires lose contact with the pavement. You should slow down and allow extra stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you prepare to drive to an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Only have to know generally where your destination is.,b:Should depend on road signs to find your way.,c:Should plan your trip in advance.
note: Plan your route in advance and review maps or directions before you start driving in unfamiliar areas.

question: Why does driving at night require increased caution?
options: a:Drivers cannot see as well at night.,b:Traffic always moves faster at night.,c:There is more volume of traffic at night.,d:Headlights are not needed after midnight.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to see hazards; headlights are required from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.

question: What does a 'No standing' sign mean at a location?
options: a:You may park there if the driver remains in the vehicle.,b:You may stop temporarily only to pickup or discharge passengers.,c:You may never stop your vehicle there.
note: A 'No standing' sign allows stopping temporarily only to load or unload passengers; parking or waiting is not permitted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with functioning lights, you should:
options: a:Follow the officer's directions rather than the traffic signal,b:Follow whatever the traffic light indicates,c:Ignore the officer and follow other drivers
note: Officer directions supersede traffic signals; obey the officer's hand signals and commands for safety and legal compliance.

question: Is it lawful for a car to share a single lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane. A car must not try to share the same lane with a motorcycle.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving are likely to:
options: a:Drive better because they are satisfied.,b:Have no driving errors.,c:Become more alert and focused.,d:Be more distracted and have trouble controlling their vehicle.
note: Eating or drinking while driving takes at least one hand off the wheel and your attention away from the road. This increases the chance of drifting in your lane, missing hazards, or reacting too slowly, so drivers are more distracted and have less control of the vehicle.

question: A broken yellow line alongside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line and prohibited from the side with the solid line. Drivers on the broken-line side may pass when it is safe; drivers on the solid-line side must not cross the line to pass.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:At your side mirror.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, you must check the blind spot in the direction you plan to move. Mirrors do not show this area. For a left lane change, quickly glance over your left shoulder after checking mirrors and signaling to be sure no vehicle is hidden beside you.

question: What type of sign is normally diamond-shaped and warns of hazards ahead?
options: a:Interstate route sign.,b:Regulatory sign,c:Warning sign.,d:School crossing sign.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are generally warning signs. They alert you to hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or merging traffic, so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

question: If you are traveling in another vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your headlights continuously.,b:Remain in the blind spot and maintain speed.,c:Sound your horn repeatedly to warn the other driver.,d:Move forward or fall back so the other driver can see you.
note: Staying in another driver’s blind spot is dangerous because they may change lanes or turn without seeing you. Either speed up to move ahead or slow down to fall back until you are visible in their mirrors, where they can more easily notice you.

question: Which safety restraints provide the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:Only an airbag.,b:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,c:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,d:Only a child restraint seat.
note: The safest protection in a crash comes from using both the lap/shoulder belt and the airbag together. Seat belts keep you properly positioned and prevent you from being thrown forward, while airbags provide extra cushioning in moderate to severe crashes. Airbags are designed to work with seat belts, not replace them, and child passengers must also be secured in appropriate child restraint seats.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you do if you are not involved?
options: a:Keep moving and pay attention to driving.,b:Keep moving without changing speed.,c:Stop to look at the scene so you can help.
note: If you are not involved in a crash, you should keep moving, focus on your driving, and watch for emergency vehicles and people near the roadway. Stopping or slowing just to look (rubbernecking) can cause additional crashes and traffic jams. Only stop if you are directly involved or if emergency help has not arrived and you can safely provide assistance without creating more danger.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, your first step should be to:
options: a:Pull up parallel to the car in front of the desired space,b:Turn your wheels immediately to the left,c:Turn your wheels to the right first
note: For standard parallel parking, you first pull up parallel to the vehicle in front of the space, leaving a safe gap and aligning your rear bumpers. Then you signal, check traffic, and begin backing into the space while turning the wheel as needed. Starting from a parallel position gives you the right angle and space to maneuver safely into the spot.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph take to stop?
options: a:50 feet,b:125 feet,c:400 feet
note: A large, fully loaded tractor‑trailer needs much more distance to stop than a passenger car. At about 55 mph, it can take roughly 400 feet—more than the length of a football field—to come to a complete stop under good conditions. This is why you should never cut closely in front of a truck and should allow extra following distance when driving near large commercial vehicles.

question: If your car begins to skid, which way should you steer?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:Turn the wheel opposite the direction of the skid.,c:Keep the front wheels straight.,d:Turn sharply into the shoulder to stop the skid.
note: When your car begins to skid, you should steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This is often described as “steering into the skid.” As the vehicle starts to straighten out, you then adjust the steering to keep control and avoid overcorrecting. Sudden or sharp steering, braking, or accelerating can make the skid worse, so make smooth, controlled inputs.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It has no effect on driving abilities.,d:It only impairs judgment at high amounts.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, reduces coordination, affects vision, and harms judgment. Even small amounts make it harder to control speed, stay in your lane, and make safe decisions, so it harms both driving skills and judgment.

question: Distracted driving is:
options: a:Extremely risky behavior,b:Common and very dangerous,c:Not a serious concern
note: Distracted driving is extremely risky because it takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. This greatly increases the chance of a crash and endangers everyone on or near the road.

question: Before backing out of a driveway near children at play, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of the vehicle and walk to the rear to ensure the way is clear.,b:Sound your horn loudly while reversing.,c:Rev the engine to get attention.,d:Rely only on mirrors to check behind you.
note: Before backing near children, walk behind your vehicle to be sure the area is clear. Children can be too small to see in mirrors or cameras and may move quickly into your path, so you must check directly before reversing.

question: Is it true that alcohol is the single greatest common factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Alcohol is a major factor in fatal crashes, but speeding is typically the single most common contributing factor in U.S. fatal crashes. While alcohol greatly increases crash risk and is involved in many deaths, it is not always the number-one factor in every year or jurisdiction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you merge onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to traffic already on the freeway.,b:Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match the speed of freeway traffic.,c:Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.,d:All of the above.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. This allows you to merge smoothly and safely without forcing other drivers to brake suddenly.

question: If your turn signals stop working, what should you use to indicate a turn?
options: a:Your horn.,b:Your headlights.,c:Hand signals.,d:Flash your emergency lights only.
note: If your electrical turn signals fail, you must use standard hand and arm signals to show other drivers when you intend to turn or slow/stop. This keeps your intentions clear and helps prevent crashes when your signal lights are not working.

question: What is the correct action when approaching railroad tracks?
options: a:Try to drive around a lowered gate.,b:Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.,c:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, you must slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Be prepared to stop if a train is approaching or warning devices are active. Never try to beat a train or go around lowered gates.

question: Which action most reliably prevents alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Simply say “No thanks, I'm driving” if offered a drink.,c:Call a taxi after you begin drinking.
note: The most reliable way to avoid an alcohol‑related crash is to decide in advance that if you drink, you will not drive. Because alcohol impairs judgment, you cannot depend on making a safe decision after you have started drinking.

question: How much longer can stopping distances be on slippery roads compared with dry pavement?
options: a:About the same as on dry pavement.,b:A little shorter than on dry pavement.,c:Two to ten times longer than on dry pavement.,d:Less than on dry pavement if you have anti-lock brakes.
note: On wet, icy, or otherwise slippery roads, your stopping distance can be many times longer than on dry pavement—often two to ten times longer. Reduce speed early and increase your following distance so you have enough room to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it unlawful to cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,b:Only when turning into a driveway.,c:When the car in front of you is disabled.,d:It is always unlawful to cross broken lines.
note: A single broken white or yellow line means you may cross it to pass or change lanes only when it is safe and will not interfere with other traffic. If crossing the line would force other drivers to slow or change position suddenly, you must not cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your car end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the one-way street.,b:In the center of the street.,c:In the right lane of the one-way street.,d:Any available lane as long as it is safe.
note: When turning left from a two‑way street onto a one‑way street, you must turn into the lane closest to you on the one‑way street, which is the left lane. This keeps you from crossing multiple lanes during the turn and reduces the risk of collision with traffic already on the one‑way street.

question: What do orange-colored signs typically indicate?
options: a:School zone signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Work zone signs.
note: Orange signs are used for temporary traffic control in work and construction zones. They warn drivers about road work, lane shifts, workers on or near the roadway, and other unusual conditions in the area.

question: Are traffic signs and pavement markings mandatory or optional?
options: a:Are merely suggestions.,b:Must always be obeyed.,c:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls and must always be obeyed. They provide instructions such as speed limits, lane use, and right‑of‑way, and ignoring them can lead to crashes and traffic citations.

question: What are the colors of warning signs indicating upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black on white.,b:Black symbols or letters on yellow.,c:White on blue.,d:Green on white.
note: Most general warning signs that alert you to upcoming hazards are yellow with black symbols or letters. These signs warn about curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, and other conditions that require extra caution.

question: If you stop along the road at night, how should you make your vehicle visible?
options: a:Turn off all your lights.,b:Use your headlights only.,c:Turn on your emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on.
note: If you must stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low‑beam headlights on. This makes your vehicle visible to other drivers without creating glare that could blind them, reducing the chance of a rear‑end collision.

question: How can you avoid drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.,b:Turning on your car radio.,c:Slowing down.
note: Stopping at regular intervals to rest, walk, and stretch is the safest and most effective way to prevent drowsiness on long trips. Radio or speed changes do not reliably keep you alert and can give a false sense of wakefulness.

question: What must you do when pedestrians are in a marked crosswalk?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.,b:No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.,c:When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.
note: When pedestrians are in a marked crosswalk, you must yield the right‑of‑way and allow them to cross safely. Slow or stop as needed so they can completely clear your lane and the adjacent lane before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:Only when other vehicles yield.,c:When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using flashing red or blue lights or a siren by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stopping until they have passed, unless otherwise directed by a police officer.

question: An arrow painted on the pavement means:
options: a:Drivers in the lane must make the movement shown by the arrow.,b:Drivers may choose whether to follow the arrow.,c:Only follow the arrow if a traffic light is not working.,d:Stop before proceeding in the arrow's direction.
note: Pavement arrows show the required direction of travel from that lane, such as left turn only or straight only. You must follow the arrow unless a traffic officer or specific sign clearly directs you to do something different.

question: What is the best way to reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep your tires properly maintained.,b:Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.,c:Watch for standing water and avoid it when safe.,d:All of the above.
note: Hydroplaning is less likely if your tires are in good condition, you reduce speed on wet or slushy roads, and you avoid standing water when it is safe to do so. Combining all of these practices gives you the best protection.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest speed strategy?
options: a:Drive at the speed of the flow of traffic within the posted limit.,b:Drive faster than the flow of traffic to avoid congestion.,c:Drive much slower than other traffic to stay safe.,d:Constantly fluctuate speed to stay alert.
note: Driving at the speed of the flow of traffic, as long as it is within the posted speed limit, is safest because it minimizes large speed differences between vehicles. Big speed differences increase the chance of rear‑end and lane‑change collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is passing you, how should you respond?
options: a:Stay in your lane and pull off the road only if necessary for safety.,b:Maintain a steady speed or slightly reduce speed to help them complete the pass safely.,c:Speed up to prevent them passing.,d:Brake suddenly to discourage them.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane, maintain a steady speed, or slightly reduce speed to help them pass safely. Do not speed up or brake suddenly. Your job is to make the pass predictable and give the other driver space to return to the lane.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway from the right lane to the left, you should:
options: a:Check mirrors, look over your left shoulder for the blind spot, signal, and then change lanes when safe.,b:Only signal and move over.,c:Rely solely on the side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors, look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter to clear your blind spot, and signal before moving. Mirrors alone cannot show vehicles in your blind spot, and signaling without checking is unsafe.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn sharply toward the curb.,b:Turn slightly to the right.,c:Turn sharply away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will rest against the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic. On an uphill without a curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about advisory or posted speed signs is correct?
options: a:They show a recommended safe speed for conditions and you should slow even more in rain, snow, or ice.,b:They are usually yellow warning signs with black lettering.,c:They indicate a maximum legal speed that must never be exceeded.
note: Advisory speed signs are yellow, usually rectangular or part of a yellow warning sign, and show a recommended safe speed for specific conditions such as curves. In rain, snow, or ice, you should slow down even more than the advisory speed; you should never ignore these signs in adverse conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who has the right-of-way when a funeral procession is present?
options: a:A pedestrian,b:The funeral procession,c:Another driver
note: Motorists, bicyclists, and pedestrians must yield to vehicles in a funeral procession; procession vehicles may follow through intersections together.

question: Anything that causes you to ____ could lead to a crash.
options: a:Take your hands off the wheel,b:Take your attention away from the task of driving,c:Take your eyes off the road
note: Anything that takes your attention away from the task of driving can lead to a crash. This includes mental distractions (daydreaming, strong emotions), visual distractions (looking at a phone or scenery), and manual distractions (reaching for objects). While taking your hands off the wheel or your eyes off the road are dangerous forms of distraction, the core safety rule is to keep your full attention on driving at all times.

question: Vehicle stopping distances never depend on which factor?
options: a:Your own reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance is affected by how quickly you react, the condition of your brakes and tires, your speed, the road surface, and vehicle weight. The time of day by itself does not directly change how far your vehicle needs to stop; it is the visibility and road conditions (such as darkness, rain, or glare) that matter, not the clock time.

question: In rain, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low-beam headlights.,b:High-beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:Hazard lights at all times.
note: In rain, you should use low-beam headlights. Low beams help you see the road and make your vehicle more visible to others without causing glare. High beams can reflect off rain, fog, or snow and actually reduce your ability to see. Parking lights or hazard lights alone are not appropriate for driving in the rain.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a vehicle to drive?
options: a:Your seat,b:The steering wheel,c:Your rearview mirror
note: Before driving, adjust your seat so you can comfortably reach the pedals, steering wheel, and controls and have a clear view of the road. Once your seating position is correct, adjust your mirrors so they properly cover the areas behind and to the sides of your vehicle, then adjust the steering wheel if needed. Your seat belt should be fastened before you start driving, but the first adjustment that affects all others is your seat position.

question: What type of situation does an orange-colored sign indicate?
options: a:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.,b:A school zone.,c:A railroad crossing.,d:A recreational area.
note: Orange signs with black letters are temporary warning signs used for construction, maintenance, and sometimes emergency operations. They alert you to changing road conditions, workers, lane shifts, or equipment ahead so you can slow down, be alert, and follow any directions.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Add extra weight to the vehicle.,b:Reduce speed and increase following distance.,c:Get off highways quickly at all costs.,d:Use only parking lights.
note: On snow or ice, your tires have much less traction, so it takes longer to stop and easier to skid. The safest technique is to slow down well below normal speeds and leave a much larger following distance so you have time and space to brake gently and steer smoothly.

question: When approaching a school bus stopped with its stop-arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Honk before passing to warn children.,c:Slow down and pass cautiously.,d:Pass on the shoulder if no children are visible.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, and it is clearly safe to move. This protects children who may be crossing the road near the bus.

question: A leaking exhaust system can cause which danger to occupants?
options: a:Make you drowsy or expose you to toxic fumes,b:Increase tire wear,c:Cause brake failure
note: A leaking exhaust can let carbon monoxide and other toxic gases enter the passenger area. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless and can make you drowsy, confused, or unconscious, and can be fatal. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Come to a full stop and proceed when it is safe.,b:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,c:Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line or before entering the crosswalk or intersection, then yield to pedestrians and other traffic. Proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus when driving on a two-lane road?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: On a standard two-lane road with one lane in each direction and no physical divider, drivers traveling in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.

question: Before driving an unfamiliar borrowed vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Hide defects to avoid embarrassing the owner.,b:Only check the radio and seat position.,c:Assume it operates the same as your car and drive immediately.,d:Take a moment to locate and test signals, lights, wipers, and brakes.
note: Before driving any unfamiliar vehicle, take a moment to adjust the seat and mirrors and locate and test the turn signals, headlights, wipers, and brakes. Knowing where these controls are and that they work properly helps you respond quickly and safely in traffic or bad weather.

question: What should you do to help prevent crashes with other road users?
options: a:Use hazards instead of turn signals.,b:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your lane.,c:Drive only on side streets.,d:Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians.
note: To help prevent crashes, make your intentions clear to others. Use turn signals before turning or changing lanes, tap your brakes to show you are slowing, use headlights and brake lights properly, and use the horn only when needed to warn others. Clear communication gives other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians time to react safely.

question: True or false: You must yield to children playing in the street.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if a parent is present,d:Only during daytime
note: Children are never permitted to play in the street, and drivers are not legally required to yield the right-of-way to someone unlawfully in the roadway. However, you must always drive at a safe speed for conditions and use extreme caution anywhere children may be present, such as neighborhoods, school zones, and near parks. Slow down, be prepared to stop suddenly, and avoid any action that could endanger a child, even if they are not using the road correctly.

question: How should a seat belt fit?
options: a:Loose across the abdomen.,b:Buckled snugly and low across your hip bones with the shoulder belt snug and comfortable across your chest.,c:Hidden under your coat for comfort.,d:Only across the chest.
note: A seat belt should fit snugly and low across the hips, touching the upper thighs, not across the soft part of the abdomen. The shoulder belt should cross the center of the chest and rest on the shoulder, not under the arm or behind the back. This positioning helps the stronger bones of your body absorb crash forces and reduces the risk of serious internal injuries.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, under which condition must you always stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted.,b:Only if flaggers are present.,c:If the crossing gate is lowered or warning lights flash.,d:Only if you hear a train.
note: You must always stop at a railroad crossing when the crossing gate is lowered or the red warning lights are flashing, because this means a train is approaching or is close enough to be a danger. You must also stop if a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible or so close that it is unsafe to cross. Never proceed until you are sure the tracks are clear and it is legal to go.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Use your high beams.,b:Use your low beams.,c:Use your parking lights.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, use low-beam headlights because they aim light downward onto the road and reduce glare that can reflect back into your eyes. High beams reflect off moisture droplets in the air and make it harder to see. Parking lights alone are not bright enough and are not a substitute for headlights.

question: What is the single most effective thing you can do to reduce injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,b:Wear your seat belt.,c:Limit your driving to weekdays.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Seat belts keep you from being thrown from the vehicle, spread crash forces over stronger parts of your body, and help you stay in position to control the vehicle during emergency maneuvers.

question: If you see an animal on the roadway, you should:
options: a:Use extreme caution and pass slowly to avoid startling it,b:Pass as close as possible,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly
note: When you see an animal on or near the roadway, slow down and use extreme caution. Pass slowly and give it as much space as safely possible so you do not startle it into moving unpredictably into your path. Never speed up or pass close to an animal, as this increases the risk of a collision.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:White.,b:Green.,c:Yellow.,d:Blue.
note: Yellow pavement markings are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A yellow centerline indicates that the lanes on each side carry traffic in different directions. White lines, by contrast, separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you do first?
options: a:Help the injured.,b:Call the police.,c:Stop immediately.
note: If you are involved in a crash, your first legal duty is to stop immediately at or near the scene. Once stopped and safe, you should move your vehicle out of traffic if possible, check for injuries, render reasonable aid, and call the police or ambulance when needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, how often must you signal?
options: a:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,b:Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.,c:Signal only when driving at night.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb, even if you do not see other traffic. Signaling lets other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians know what you intend to do so they can react safely.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what is your first legal obligation?
options: a:Stop.,b:Call the police.,c:Determine if anyone is injured.
note: In any serious crash, your first legal obligation is to stop at or near the scene and remain there. After stopping, you must check for injuries, call 911 if anyone is hurt or the crash is serious, and comply with any required crash-reporting laws in your state.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a motorist is making a left turn at an intersection, must they yield to an oncoming bicyclist?
options: a:False: Bicyclists must yield.,b:Only at marked bike lanes.,c:Only if the bicyclist is on the sidewalk.,d:True: Yes, yield to oncoming bicyclists.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, including bicyclists. Bicycles on the roadway have the same right-of-way as other vehicles, so you must wait for an oncoming bicyclist to pass if they are close enough to be a hazard.

question: Which statement is true about alcohol's effect on driving abilities?
options: a:Only very high BAC reduces concentration.,b:Alcohol does not reduce concentration.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.,d:Small amounts improve reaction time.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can affect the brain, reducing concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. These changes make it harder to notice hazards, make good decisions, and react in time, which is why any drinking can impair driving.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:Provide information for drivers.,b:Are usually not important.,c:Are only found in construction zones.
note: Pavement markings are critical safety devices. They show lane boundaries, where passing is allowed, where you must stop, and warn of upcoming conditions such as school zones or railroad crossings. Drivers must understand and obey these markings to stay in the correct lane and avoid collisions.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what is the safest response?
options: a:Pull up beside them and confront them.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Flash your high beams repeatedly to warn them.,d:Follow closely to teach them a lesson.
note: When another driver cuts you off, reacting aggressively increases the risk of a crash and road rage. The safest choice is to stay calm, create space by slowing slightly if needed, and continue driving defensively. Avoid eye contact, gestures, or confrontations so the situation does not escalate.

question: If your vehicle hits an unattended parked car and you cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a written note with your name, address, and the circumstances of the accident, and follow any required reporting laws.,b:Drive away after reporting it when convenient.,c:Wait for the police to arrive regardless.
note: If you collide with an unattended vehicle, leave your contact information and details of the incident where the owner can find it.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your bloodstream, what happens?
options: a:It speeds up your reactions.,b:It makes you more cautious.,c:It metabolizes faster improving coordination.,d:It makes you overconfident and slows reactions.
note: As alcohol builds up in your bloodstream, it slows your reaction time, reduces coordination, and impairs judgment. Many people feel more confident or less inhibited, which makes them more likely to take risks while actually being less able to react and control the vehicle safely.

question: True or false: Since driving involves risk, you should continually improve driving and observation skills.
options: a:Only if you are a new driver.,b:Only for professional drivers,c:False,d:True
note: Driving always involves some risk, so all drivers—not just beginners or professionals—should keep improving their observation, anticipation, and vehicle-handling skills. Practicing defensive driving and staying alert to changing road and traffic conditions helps reduce the chance of a collision.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Keep driving in your lane at a reduced speed.,b:Slow down and continue if it is in another lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop until it passes.,d:Speed up to get out of its way.
