note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it has passed, unless otherwise directed by law enforcement. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can move quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:Only on multi-lane highways.,b:Only during poor weather.,c:Only when behind a school bus.,d:On hills or curves with limited visibility, at intersections, on bridges, and at railroad crossings, or where signs or markings prohibit passing.
note: Passing is unsafe and generally prohibited where your view of oncoming traffic is limited or where conflicts are likely. You must not pass on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, at intersections or railroad crossings where other traffic may enter, on bridges or in tunnels where space is limited, or anywhere signs or pavement markings prohibit passing.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, which action is recommended?
options: a:Sit in the car and wait without signaling.,b:Use your four-way flashers, pull off the road if possible, and signal before exiting.,c:Sound your horn to attract attention.,d:Stop in the travel lane until help arrives.
note: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, first signal and carefully move as far off the roadway as possible, preferably onto the right shoulder. Turn on your four-way (hazard) flashers so other drivers can see you. Once stopped, make sure it is safe before exiting the vehicle, and raise the hood or place warning devices if available to show that your vehicle is disabled.

question: If you have a tire blowout, what is the correct sequence of actions?
options: a:Brake hard immediately and pull off quickly.,b:Take your foot off the gas, do not brake immediately, gradually slow and pull off the road.,c:Accelerate to stabilize the vehicle.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply to the shoulder.
note: During a tire blowout, a sudden brake or sharp steering can cause loss of control. Instead, firmly grip the steering wheel, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking until the car has slowed, then gently brake as needed and steer smoothly to a safe place off the road before stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it required to use your turn signal?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.,d:All of the above.
note: Turn signals must be used any time you intend to change the vehicle’s direction or position on the road. This includes changing lanes, turning, pulling into or out of a parking space, and entering traffic from a parking area, driveway, or alley. Signaling early and clearly lets other drivers know what you plan to do so they can react safely.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When you park facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will gently touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may drivers use a cell phone while driving?
options: a:Only when using a cell phone in a manner allowed by state law (often hands-free and never for texting),b:Never under any circumstances,c:At any time in any manner
note: In most U.S. states, drivers may use a cell phone while driving only if it is used in a legal, safe manner. Handheld use and texting are often restricted or banned, especially for younger drivers, but hands‑free use is generally allowed. However, some states allow limited handheld use for adults, and emergency calls are usually permitted even where handheld use is banned.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Defending yourself against poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.,c:Following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning for hazards, anticipating what other road users might do, and adjusting your speed and position early to avoid conflicts. This includes keeping a safe following distance, obeying speed limits, and being prepared to react to mistakes by other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When interacting with pedestrians, which is required of drivers?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,b:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle.,c:Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.
note: Drivers must always do whatever is necessary to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally or not paying attention. You still have a duty to slow down, stop, or change lanes to prevent a collision, because pedestrians are much more vulnerable than people in vehicles.

question: Should the stereo volume be so loud that you cannot hear traffic?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You should always keep the stereo volume low enough that you can clearly hear horns, sirens, and other traffic sounds. Being able to hear what is happening around your vehicle is an important part of staying aware and reacting quickly to emergencies.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed you are traveling.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The pavement condition.,d:All of the above.
note: Braking distance is how far your vehicle travels after you apply the brakes until it stops. It increases with higher speed, worn or poorly maintained brakes and tires, and poor pavement conditions such as wet, icy, or gravel surfaces. Vehicle weight and downhill grades also increase braking distance. Reaction time affects total stopping distance, not the braking distance itself.

question: If an officer suspects you of driving under the influence, what is true about testing?
options: a:Can always refuse to be tested for the presence of controlled substances.,b:Can refuse to be tested for the presence of substances if it is your first offense.,c:May physically refuse testing, but implied consent laws treat refusal as a violation that carries serious penalties, including license revocation.
note: Under Nevada’s implied consent law, by driving on public roads you have already agreed to submit to chemical testing (breath, blood, or urine) when lawfully arrested or detained for suspected DUI. You may physically refuse the test, but that refusal is not a protected right and leads to serious penalties such as license revocation and possible use of reasonable force to obtain a sample. You should comply with required testing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles already on the public road,b:Expect drivers on the road to yield to them,c:Force their way into traffic if necessary
note: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all traffic already on the roadway, including vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians. Enter only when there is a large enough gap so you do not force other road users to slow or change lanes suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually the best practice?
options: a:Accelerate to a speed that matches the speed of traffic, without exceeding the speed limit.,b:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
note: When using a freeway on‑ramp, you should use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic on the freeway as closely as possible, without exceeding the speed limit. This makes it easier and safer to merge into a gap. Vehicles already on the freeway have the right‑of‑way, so adjust your speed and merge when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which factor greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Slow speeds.,b:Driving in rain only.,c:Night driving.,d:High speeds.
note: High speeds greatly increase both the distance needed to stop and the force of a crash. Because kinetic energy increases with the square of speed, even a small increase in speed can make collisions much more severe and give you far less time and space to react.

question: On a one-way street when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop,b:Speed up to get out of the way,c:Turn on your hazard lights and continue driving
note: On a one-way street, you still must yield to emergency vehicles using lights or siren. Move safely toward the nearest edge of the roadway—right or left—and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by officials.

question: If you are being tailgated and there is no right lane, how should you react?
options: a:Speed up so the tailgater goes around you.,b:Stop in your lane immediately.,c:Slow down when safe to create space ahead and encourage them to pass.,d:Brake abruptly to warn them.
note: When being tailgated and you cannot move to the right, the safest response is to gradually slow down when it is safe. This increases the space in front of you, reduces the risk of a sudden stop, and often encourages the tailgater to pass when they have a safe opportunity. Never brake abruptly or speed up.

question: When may you use a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane?
options: a:When towing a trailer.,b:When you are driving faster than other traffic.,c:When driving more slowly than traffic.,d:When your vehicle has multiple occupants.
note: HOV (carpool) lanes are reserved for vehicles that meet the minimum occupancy shown on the signs, usually two or more people. They are marked with diamond symbols and special signs. You may use them only when your vehicle meets the posted occupancy or other posted requirements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a steady yellow traffic light?
options: a:Continue at the same speed because you have the right-of-way.,b:Stop immediately even if in the intersection.,c:Accelerate to clear the intersection before it turns red.,d:Slow to a stop unless you are already within the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection or so close that stopping would be unsafe, continue through carefully rather than braking hard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: At an uncontrolled (open) intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the right may proceed first when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,b:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.,c:Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
note: On a two-lane road with oncoming traffic, you should only return to your lane after passing when there is plenty of space between you and the vehicle you passed. A good rule is to wait until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle (or its headlights at night) in your rearview mirror before moving back. This ensures you do not cut too closely in front of the other driver and that you have enough room to slow or stop if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a shared center lane be used on a roadway with traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:To pass other vehicles.,b:To slow down or stop before making a left turn.,c:As an additional travel lane when traffic is slow.
note: A shared center lane (center left-turn lane) is for vehicles from either direction to slow down, wait, and then make a left turn or a permitted U-turn. It is not a passing lane and must not be used as a regular travel lane. Using it only for turning helps prevent head-on collisions and keeps through traffic flowing smoothly.

question: Which of the following is an effect of consuming alcoholic beverages?
options: a:It impairs thinking, reaction time, and coordination.,b:It improves night vision.,c:It sharpens judgment.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and nervous system functions. Even small amounts can reduce judgment, slow reaction time, and affect coordination and balance. It can also blur vision and make it harder to track moving objects or see clearly at night. Because safe driving depends on quick decisions and precise control, any impairment from alcohol makes driving dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what is true?
options: a:You may still turn in the arrow's direction but must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic,b:You may turn with absolute right-of-way,c:You may no longer turn in that direction under any circumstance
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn, meaning oncoming traffic is stopped. When the green arrow goes away and a solid green light remains, you may still turn in that direction, but it becomes an unprotected turn. You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians in the crosswalk and only turn when it is safe and clear.

question: Which of the following statements about winter driving is not true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:Checking your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels is especially important during the winter.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.
note: Winter driving is challenging because snow, ice, and cold temperatures reduce traction and can affect how your vehicle runs. It is especially important to check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid so your engine is protected and your windshield stays clear. You should not use cruise control on snow, ice, or in heavy rain because you need full control of your speed and may need to adjust quickly to changing traction.

question: Regulatory signs are used to:
options: a:Indicate what drivers must or must not do in a designated area,b:Warn of potential hazards ahead,c:Provide directions to nearby services
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do or must not do by law in that specific area, such as obeying speed limits, stopping, yielding, or not turning. Ignoring these signs can result in traffic violations because they communicate legal requirements, not just guidance or warnings.

question: When driving in fog, should you use your high beam headlights?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: In fog, you should use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams, and fog lights if your vehicle has them, help you see the road and help others see you without creating extra glare.

question: Which of the following does NOT occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You become more alert.,d:Your ability to recover from headlight glare is reduced.
note: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time, makes it harder to judge speed and distance, and reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare. It does not make you more alert; instead, it impairs your thinking and coordination, which is why driving after drinking is so dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A green arrow pointing left,c:A solid green light.
note: A steady green arrow pointing left means you have a protected left turn: oncoming traffic is stopped, and you have the right-of-way to turn left. With a solid green light, you may turn left only when it is safe and after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: When changing lanes, what actions are important?
options: a:Signal, check your blind spot, and ensure the lane is clear before moving,b:Only signal and immediately move,c:Make a sudden lane change to avoid slow traffic
note: Before changing lanes, always signal to let others know your intention, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move when you are sure the lane is clear and you have enough space, making the lane change smooth and predictable for other drivers.

question: How can you avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Rely solely on mirrors to check blind spots.,b:Honk briefly before moving.,c:Quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder before changing lanes.,d:Adjust your mirrors every mile.
note: Checking blind spots requires a quick head turn over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move. Mirrors alone cannot show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, so you must glance over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

question: What is hardest to see at night?
options: a:Other motorists.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Road signs.
note: At night, pedestrians are much harder to see than other vehicles or reflective road signs. Headlights and streetlights often illuminate cars and signs well, but people walking or standing may wear dark clothing and have no lights or reflectors, making them the hardest to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a 'No stopping' sign permit you to do?
options: a:To discharge passengers.,b:To avoid conflict with other traffic.,c:Long enough to unload packages.
note: A 'No stopping' sign means you may not stop your vehicle at the curb or roadside except when required to obey a traffic control device, follow a police officer’s directions, or avoid a conflict with other traffic. You may not stop there just to load or unload passengers or packages.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield only to traffic on your right,b:Always make a complete stop even when no traffic is present,c:Slow and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection or roadway
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Yield the right-of-way to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection or close enough on the roadway you are entering to be a hazard. Proceed only when it is safe and you will not interfere with other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, what should you generally do to your speed?
options: a:Reduce speed so you can remain in control and stay in your lane,b:Increase speed to complete the turn faster,c:Maintain the exact same speed
note: Before turning, slow down to a safe speed so you can stay in your lane and maintain full control of the vehicle. Enter the turn at a reduced speed, then gently accelerate as you complete the turn if conditions allow. Turning too fast can cause you to drift out of your lane or lose traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:By looking in your side mirrors.,b:By looking in your rearview mirror.,c:By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Before changing lanes, you must signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly turn your head to look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check lets you see vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that may be hidden in your blind spot.

question: How should you safely pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Honk continuously before passing,b:Drive into the bicycle lane to pass more quickly,c:Slow down and give as much lateral space as possible
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them as much space as safely possible. Many states require at least 3 feet of clearance, and more is safer at higher speeds. Do not honk aggressively or drive into a bike lane to pass; instead, wait until it is safe, move well into the adjacent lane, and pass at a cautious speed.

question: True or False: Ramps and bridges freeze before the main highway and road surfaces.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Ramps and bridges freeze before the main roadway because cold air surrounds them from above and below, causing the surface temperature to drop faster. In freezing or near‑freezing conditions, reduce speed and avoid sudden braking or steering when driving on bridges, overpasses, and ramps.

question: Must you stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, regardless of whether the road is public or private, unless a specific state law clearly provides an exception. Stopping allows children to cross safely, and passing a stopped school bus in this situation is illegal and extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate and changing lanes, what must you do?
options: a:Change lanes without signaling in light traffic.,b:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.,c:Always use cruise control when changing lanes.,d:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
note: On an interstate, before changing lanes you must signal, check your mirrors, and then check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder. Make lane changes only when necessary and safe. The shoulder is for emergencies only, and cruise control has nothing to do with the basic lane‑change procedure.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a fire engine is following you but not using its emergency signals, how should you respond?
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Stop as quickly as you can.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If a fire engine or other emergency vehicle is behind you but is not using its lights or siren, it is operating as a regular vehicle. You are not required to pull over or clear the lane; instead, continue driving normally, obeying all traffic laws and maintaining safe following distance and speed.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Drivers may change lanes or pass across a broken white line when it is legal and safe, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling properly.

question: If you see a lane with a solid line on your side and a broken line on the other, may you pass?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A solid line on your side of the road means you must not pass; it indicates that passing from your lane is unsafe, such as near hills, curves, or intersections. The side with the broken line is allowed to pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: Which actions help you drive safely at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance and make sure headlights are working properly.,b:Drive with no headlights to reduce glare.,c:Always use high beams regardless of oncoming traffic.,d:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of visibility.
note: At night, visibility is reduced and it is harder to judge distance and speed. Increasing your following distance gives you more time to react, and making sure your headlights and other lights work properly helps you see and be seen. Use high beams only when appropriate and dim them for oncoming traffic or when following another vehicle closely.

question: A sound rule for passing is to:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and safe,b:Pass on the right whenever possible,c:Always try to get to the front of slow traffic
note: Safe passing means going with the general flow of traffic and passing only when it is legal, necessary, and clearly safe. You should never weave through traffic or pass on the right except where specifically allowed, such as on multi-lane roads when another vehicle is in the left lane.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drive as you would normally since emotions don't affect driving.,b:Drive faster to get where you are going quickly.,c:Listen to loud music to feel better while driving.,d:Take time to calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
note: Strong emotions like anger, anxiety, or crying reduce your concentration, slow your reaction time, and make you more likely to take risks. Before driving, you should calm yourself, regain focus, and only start the engine when you can give full attention to the road.

question: What helps you avoid emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Honk to warn drivers ahead.,b:Look ahead and keep a safe following distance.,c:Drive only in the right lane.,d:Constantly change lanes to avoid slowdowns.
note: Looking well ahead and keeping a safe following distance gives you more time to see problems early and slow down gradually. This reduces the need for sudden emergency stops and lowers the risk of rear‑end collisions.

question: How can you relieve fatigue during a long drive?
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours.,b:Chew gum continuously.,c:Drive with one eye closed at a time.,d:Open all windows and drive faster.
note: On long trips, stopping every couple of hours to get out, walk, and rest helps prevent fatigue. If you feel drowsy, the safest choice is to pull off the road in a safe place and rest or stop driving for the day.

question: Which activities can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,b:Talking or texting on a phone.,c:Changing radio stations or CDs.,d:All of the above.
note: Anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving—such as eating, using a phone, or adjusting music—can distract you and increase crash risk. You should minimize these activities and focus on the road.

question: Is it unlawful to drive at night using only parking lights?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Parking lights are not bright enough for driving and are not a substitute for headlights. At night or when visibility is poor, the law requires you to use your headlights so you can see the road and other drivers can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you allow?
options: a:Always back up to the nearest driveway.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,d:Demand the other driver pull over.
note: On a narrow road, you must share the roadway so each vehicle has about half of the main‑traveled portion. This lets both vehicles pass safely without forcing either driver completely off the road or into a dangerous maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At an intersection with a stop sign.,b:Where there is a red light.,c:When a traffic officer orders you to stop.,d:In all of these situations.
note: You must come to a complete stop at stop signs, at red traffic lights (including flashing red), and any time a police officer or other authorized person directing traffic orders you to stop.

question: If other drivers around you are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, do not retaliate, and distance yourself from the situation.,b:Make eye contact to assert yourself.,c:Respond with hand gestures.
note: When other drivers show signs of road rage, the safest response is to avoid eye contact, do not react or retaliate, and create space between your vehicle and theirs. Slow down, change lanes, or exit the roadway when safe so you are no longer near the aggressive driver.

question: What may occur when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:Nothing will happen.,b:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be increased.,c:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be reduced.
note: Alcohol combined with many drugs, including some prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines, can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment more than either substance alone. The combined effects can be stronger and more dangerous than expected.

question: What does a steady green light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:Stop and wait for cross traffic.,b:Proceed through the intersection if the way is clear and turn if permitted.,c:Always turn without yielding.,d:Reverse out of the intersection.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn when it is safe, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic when turning left. Green never gives you the right to move without checking and yielding where required.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light means you should:
options: a:Increase speed to clear the intersection.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Yield to oncoming traffic only.,d:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means the signal is warning you to use extra caution, not to stop. You should slow down, look carefully for other vehicles, pedestrians, or hazards, and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: The space you require to cross traffic depends on:
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic,b:Whether there is a stop sign,c:Whether you used your turn signal
note: When crossing traffic, you must judge the size of the gap you need based on how fast other vehicles are coming, how far away they are, and how road and weather conditions affect your ability to accelerate and clear the intersection safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, must drivers yield to motorists who arrived before them?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: At a four‑way stop, drivers must yield to vehicles that arrive first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. This order of arrival rule helps keep the intersection safe and predictable.

question: Is it legal to drive through, around, or under a railroad gate or barrier?
options: a:False,b:True
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive through, around, or under a lowered railroad gate or barrier. You must stop and wait until the gates are fully raised and the warning signals have stopped before crossing the tracks.

question: Roads freeze most quickly where they are:
options: a:Shaded by trees or buildings (in the sun they may stay warmer),b:Flat and exposed to full sun,c:Curvy with lots of traffic
note: Shaded areas of the road freeze first and thaw last because they receive less sunlight. Bridges, overpasses, and shaded spots can stay icy even when other parts of the road look clear, so you should slow down and use extra caution in these areas during cold weather.

question: Distracted drivers are at greater crash risk when using which device?
options: a:Cell phone,b:Radio,c:CD player
note: Cell phones, including hands‑free, are among the most distracting devices because they take your eyes, hands, and mind away from driving. While radios and CD players can distract you, phone use is strongly associated with a higher crash risk, so you should avoid using a cell phone while driving whenever possible.

question: If a vehicle equipped with ABS starts to skid on a slippery road, what should the driver do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal.
note: With ABS, you should press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer where you want to go. The system automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent wheel lockup. Do not pump the brakes yourself in an ABS‑equipped vehicle, because that interferes with the system’s ability to work properly.

question: How close may you legally park to a crosswalk?
options: a:20 feet,b:40 feet,c:30 feet
note: In many states, you may not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, but a common standard distance used on exams is 30 feet to keep crosswalks clear and pedestrians visible. Always leave ample space before a crosswalk so drivers can see people entering or using it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do before passing on a multilane highway?
options: a:Pass only on the right.,b:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,c:Watch for oncoming traffic.
note: Before passing on a multilane highway, make sure the lane you will move into is clear and that you have enough space to pass safely. Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, change lanes smoothly, and then return to your lane only when it is safe. Passing is usually done on the left; passing on the right is allowed only in specific, clearly safe situations.

question: Are headlights legally required when people or vehicles cannot be seen at 1,000 feet?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must use headlights from about half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise and any time you cannot clearly see people or vehicles at 1,000 feet. Turning on your headlights in low‑visibility conditions helps you see and also makes your vehicle more visible to others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a yield sign, you must:
options: a:Slow down and yield to pedestrians and traffic, stopping if necessary,b:Always come to a complete stop even if the way is clear,c:Have automatic right-of-way
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be ready to stop. You must yield to pedestrians and to any traffic that has the right-of-way, and only proceed when it is safe. A complete stop is required if other road users would be affected.

question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is most likely:
options: a:A crossing guard.,b:A deaf person.,c:Part of a traffic study.,d:A blind person.
note: A white cane or a guide dog identifies a pedestrian who is blind or visually impaired. Drivers must always yield the right-of-way, use extra caution, and never honk or block their path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: For how far may drivers travel in a center turn lane before making a left turn?
options: a:About 100–200 feet, or only as far as needed to safely prepare for the turn.,b:Up to 500 feet.,c:There is no distance limit; it may be used as a travel lane.
note: A center left‑turn lane is for preparing and making left turns, not for through travel. In many states, you may not drive more than about 200 feet in this lane before beginning your turn, and you should enter it only close enough to the turn to safely slow and complete the maneuver.

question: How are crosswalks indicated?
options: a:Always indicated by vertical pavement markings.,b:Always indicated by horizontal pavement markings.,c:Either indicated by pavement markings or are not marked at all.
note: Crosswalks at intersections may be marked with painted lines or may be unmarked, but pedestrians still have the right-of-way in both. Drivers must yield to pedestrians in any crosswalk, marked or unmarked.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive at a speed that is:
options: a:The maximum speed limit.,b:Faster than is reasonable and prudent.,c:Safe for existing conditions.
note: You must never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for current conditions, even if that is below the posted speed limit. Adjust your speed for weather, traffic, road surface, and visibility so you can stop safely if hazards appear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Coming to a complete stop, yielding to cross traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when clear describes the meaning of which signal?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, you must yield to any cross traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: In fog, which headlight use is correct?
options: a:Use low beams and drive cautiously; do not use high beams,b:Use high beams to see farther ahead,c:Turn off headlights and use parking lights
note: In fog, always use low-beam headlights (or fog lights if equipped). High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can create glare, making it harder to see. Slow down, increase following distance, and be prepared for sudden hazards.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash over a black symbol mean?
options: a:Drivers must stop.,b:The action shown is forbidden.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.
note: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a diagonal slash over a black symbol means that the action shown by the symbol is prohibited. For example, a right-turn arrow with a red circle and slash means no right turn is allowed at that location.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your four-way flashers.,c:Turn on your headlights (low beam),d:Do not use any lights.
note: You must turn on headlights at dusk or in poor visibility and use low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and 500 feet when following another vehicle.

question: What should you do when driving in foggy conditions?
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights.,c:It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: In fog, use low-beam headlights so the light aims down at the road instead of reflecting back at you. Reduce your speed, increase following distance, and be ready to stop if visibility becomes too poor. High beams and hazard lights are not appropriate for normal driving in fog.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It prevents drivers from changing lanes.,b:It eliminates the need for mirrors.,c:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,d:It increases travel speed.
note: Maintaining a space cushion gives you extra time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake, a hazard appears, or traffic suddenly slows. This buffer helps you brake, steer, or change lanes more safely and reduces the chance of rear-end or sideswipe collisions.

question: On non-freeway roads, drivers should look at least how many seconds ahead?
options: a:12 seconds,b:5 seconds,c:10 seconds
note: Looking about 12 seconds ahead on non-freeway roads helps you spot hazards early, such as slowing traffic, pedestrians, or road work. By scanning farther ahead, you can adjust your speed or lane smoothly instead of making sudden, unsafe maneuvers.

question: On a road that has no sidewalks, which direction should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:In the same direction as the traffic flow.,b:On the side where traffic is lightest.,c:In the middle of the lane to be more visible.,d:On the side facing oncoming traffic.
note: When there is no sidewalk, pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic. This lets them see approaching vehicles and move out of the way if needed, which is safer than having traffic come from behind.

question: If railroad crossing signals are flashing as you approach, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Look for a train and then speed up to clear the track.,c:Proceed if no train is visible.,d:Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail while the signals warn of a train.
note: Flashing railroad crossing signals mean a train is approaching. You must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and remain stopped until the signals stop and it is clearly safe to cross. Never try to beat a train or go around lowered gates.

question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars.,b:You may miss their turn signals.,c:It reduces your fuel efficiency.,d:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle in front slows or stops suddenly.
note: If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or distance to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Keeping a safe following distance gives you room to brake smoothly and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

question: What is the most common color used for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Warning signs are most often yellow with black symbols or lettering and are usually diamond-shaped. They alert drivers to upcoming conditions such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings so you can adjust speed and position in advance.

question: How should you scan the road to prepare for hazards ahead?
options: a:Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.,b:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.,c:Stare straight ahead at all times.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan far ahead, to the sides, and check mirrors so they can spot hazards early and have time to react. You should not rest your foot on the brake pedal or stare straight ahead; both reduce your awareness of changing conditions around you.

question: How does distracted driving usually affect your reaction to hazards?
options: a:It improves focus on driving tasks.,b:It has no effect.,c:It makes you react faster.,d:It causes you to react more slowly.
note: When you are distracted, your attention is divided and you notice hazards later. This usually makes your reactions slower and less accurate, which greatly increases the chance of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit indicate?
options: a:The maximum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.,c:The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed allowed on that road when conditions are ideal. In rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility, you must slow down below the posted limit if that speed would be unsafe, because you are always required to drive at a speed that is safe for current conditions.

question: Which practice does NOT help promote safe night driving?
options: a:Relying on tinted windows that reduce night visibility,b:Keeping the windshield clean,c:Carrying a flashlight
note: Tinted windows that are too dark reduce how much you can see at night and make driving more dangerous. For safer night driving, keep your windshield and windows clean to reduce glare and improve visibility, and having a flashlight in the vehicle can help you see outside the car if you must stop in the dark.

question: If you must slow on a slippery road, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: On a slippery road, sudden braking can cause your wheels to lock and your vehicle to skid. The safest first action is to gently take your foot off the accelerator so the car slows down gradually. If you need to slow more, apply the brakes smoothly and steadily, not abruptly.

question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms out the window.,b:Sound your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians.,c:Use your emergency lights only.,d:Shout at the other driver.
note: When you see a collision is likely, you should use your horn to quickly warn the other driver or nearby pedestrians. A short, sharp blast of the horn can get attention faster than any other signal and may give others time to react and avoid the crash.

question: What do pennant-shaped signs indicate?
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.,d:Speed limits.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are placed on the left side of the road to mark the beginning of a no-passing zone. They work with the pavement markings to tell you that it is unsafe and illegal to pass other vehicles in that area.

question: What color are signs that show distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Green with white letters.,b:Yellow with black letters.,c:Red with white letters.,d:Blue with white letters.
note: Guide signs that show destinations, directions, and distances on highways are green with white letters or symbols. These signs help you know how far it is to the next exit or city and which lane or exit you should use.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Are passing a bicyclist.,b:See a child who is about to run into the street.,c:Are traveling through an intersection.
note: You should use your horn to help prevent collisions, such as when you are passing a bicyclist and need to make sure they are aware of your vehicle. A light tap on the horn can alert them without startling them. You may also use your horn to warn others of immediate danger, but you should not use it routinely at every intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cross lanes to reach the exit.,b:Make a U-turn on the interstate.,c:Continue to the next exit and use it to return.,d:Reverse on the shoulder to the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, stay calm, keep going, and take the next exit. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to stop, back up, make a U‑turn, or swerve suddenly across lanes on a freeway. Use the next exit to safely turn around and return to your intended route.

question: What is a key trait of a good defensive driver?
options: a:Keeping a constant speed regardless of conditions.,b:Showing impatience with slow drivers.,c:Driving slowly at all times.,d:Anticipating and watching for actions of other drivers.
note: A good defensive driver constantly scans the road and anticipates what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists might do. By expecting possible mistakes from others and being ready to react, you can avoid many collisions. Speed and attitude should always be adjusted to conditions, not kept constant or driven aggressively.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won't endanger your driving?
options: a:Know how any medications affect your driving.,b:Drive despite physical limitations to maintain schedule.,c:Ignore prescribed limits.,d:Only drive when perfectly fit every day.
note: To drive safely, you must understand how your physical condition and any medications affect your ability to operate a vehicle. Some prescriptions and over‑the‑counter drugs can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. Follow your doctor’s and pharmacist’s advice and only drive when you are fit to do so.

question: Does a double solid yellow centerline permit passing in either direction?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: A double solid yellow centerline means traffic in both directions must stay in its lane and may not cross the lines to pass. You may usually cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but not to overtake another vehicle.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Keep wheels straight ahead.,b:Turn wheels sharply away from the curb.,c:Turn your wheels to the left toward traffic.,d:Turn your wheels to the right toward the curb.
note: When parking facing downhill on a two‑way street with a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb (to the right). If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic. Always set the parking brake as well.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.,b:Oncoming traffic.,c:Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.,d:Both oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians already in or entering the crosswalk. Drivers already in the intersection and other road users proceeding straight or turning right generally have the right-of-way over a left‑turning vehicle.

question: Which of these statements about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You never have to stop at a railroad crossing,b:You may always drive around a gate if no train is visible,c:Not all crossings have gates or signals, and it is illegal to go around lowered gates
note: Many railroad crossings do not have gates or flashing signals, so you must always look and listen for trains. When gates are present and lowered, it is both illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around them, even if you do not see a train.

question: Which is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers,b:Human error,c:Bad weather
note: Most crashes are caused by human error, such as distraction, speeding, following too closely, misjudging gaps, or ignoring traffic laws. While weather and road conditions can contribute, driver behavior is the primary factor in the majority of collisions.

question: About how many standard alcoholic drinks does the average body eliminate per hour?
options: a:Three drinks an hour.,b:One drink an hour.,c:Two drinks an hour.
note: A common guideline is that the body eliminates the alcohol in about one standard drink per hour, but this varies widely with body size, sex, food intake, health, and other factors. You can still be impaired even if you drink less than this rate, so never rely on this rule to decide if you are safe to drive.

question: What should you do before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe to do so.,b:Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.,c:Cross especially quickly when a train is approaching.
note: Before crossing railroad tracks, slow down, look carefully in both directions, and listen for trains. Obey all signals and stop if lights are flashing, gates are down, or a train is approaching. Cross only when you are sure it is safe and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

question: Signs that warn of hazardous conditions ahead are called:
options: a:Guide signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Warning signs.,d:Information signs.
note: Warning signs are yellow (or fluorescent yellow-green in some areas) and are used to alert drivers to hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings. They do not give instructions like regulatory signs; they warn you so you can adjust speed and position for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Yield to vehicles approaching from the right and be prepared to yield to avoid a crash.,c:Stop at the intersection regardless of traffic.,d:Always let the largest vehicle go first.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), you must slow, be ready to stop, and yield the right‑of‑way to any vehicle already in the intersection and to vehicles approaching from your right. You should also be prepared to yield to avoid a collision, even if you technically have the right‑of‑way.

question: When the road is marked with a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:If traffic is clear.
note: A solid yellow line with a broken yellow line means passing is allowed only for the side with the broken line. If the broken line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass, but only when there is no oncoming traffic and you can complete the pass safely without exceeding the speed limit.

question: How should you approach turns when roads are slick?
options: a:Change lanes quickly.,b:Accelerate quickly.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual.
note: On slick roads, such as when it is raining, icy, or covered with wet leaves, your tires have less traction. You should slow down before and during turns so you can steer smoothly and avoid skidding. Sudden acceleration, braking, or sharp steering can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?
options: a:See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.,b:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights and/or a siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right as safely possible and stopping until it has passed. This creates a clear path so emergency responders can reach the scene quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop and ensuring it is safe to proceed.,b:After slowing down to verify no cross traffic.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.,d:Without stopping if no other cars are present.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. After stopping, look for traffic and pedestrians in all directions and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Must drivers yield to pedestrians even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly?
options: a:Yes. Drivers must use due care and yield or stop if needed to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
note: Drivers must use due care to avoid hitting pedestrians at all times, even when pedestrians are careless or crossing improperly. You must slow, yield, or stop if necessary to prevent a collision, regardless of whether the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.

question: Why must you use extra caution near a pedestrian using a white cane?
options: a:They may be deaf.,b:They are likely a police officer.,c:They are visually impaired and may not see your vehicle.,d:They will always yield to cars.
note: A white cane (with or without a red tip) or a guide dog identifies a blind or visually impaired pedestrian. They may not see your vehicle or be able to judge its speed, so you must slow down, yield the right‑of‑way, and be prepared to stop.

question: When stopped in a line crossing a railroad track with no signals, what must you ensure before entering the tracks?
options: a:You have enough space ahead to clear the tracks without stopping.,b:You have the right-of-way and can proceed.,c:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,d:You should speed across quickly.
note: Never enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough space on the far side to completely clear the tracks without stopping. Stopping on the tracks is extremely dangerous, and you must not pass other vehicles as you approach or cross railroad tracks.

question: When might you drive slower than the posted speed limit?
options: a:Whenever weather, visibility, road surface, or traffic conditions make the posted speed unsafe.,b:Only on winding roads, regardless of conditions.,c:Only in heavy traffic, even if conditions are otherwise ideal.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the limit whenever weather, visibility, road surface, or traffic conditions make the posted speed unsafe, such as in rain, snow, fog, or on icy or gravel roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you not omit when changing lanes?
options: a:Check side and rearview mirrors.,b:Use a turn signal to indicate your intentions.,c:Check for other drivers also moving into the same lane.,d:Ignore blind spots and rely on mirrors only.
note: When changing lanes, you must always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots while also being aware of other vehicles that may be moving into the same lane. Relying only on mirrors and ignoring blind spots is dangerous because vehicles can be hidden in areas your mirrors do not show.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage change how alcohol affects reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Hard ciders and mixed drinks always have greater effects.,b:Wine affects reflexes less than liquor.,c:Yes, beer affects you less than wine.,d:No, the type does not change the impairment—only the amount consumed.
note: Alcohol affects reflexes and judgment based mainly on how much alcohol you consume, how quickly you drink it, your body size, and other personal factors. A standard serving of beer, wine, or liquor contains about the same amount of pure alcohol, so any type can impair you equally if the alcohol amount is the same.

question: True or false: Orange signs are used to warn drivers in construction work zones.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only at night,d:Only on highways
note: Orange signs are used for temporary traffic control in construction and maintenance work zones. They warn drivers of changing road conditions, workers, lane shifts, and reduced speeds so that drivers can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

question: A flashing red traffic signal requires the same action as:
options: a:Stopping at a stop sign,b:Slowing as at a yield sign,c:Continuing through without stopping
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in or approaching the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure before changing lanes on a multilane highway?
options: a:Reduce your speed before changing lanes.,b:Sound your horn before changing lanes.,c:Signal, check mirrors and blind spot, then change lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, signal to show your intention, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Change lanes only when there is enough space and it is clearly safe to move.

question: If involved in an accident, what actions should a driver take?
options: a:Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.,c:Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.,d:All of the above.
note: After a crash, you must stop at or near the scene, make sure you are not standing in traffic where you could be hit, and turn off the ignitions of damaged vehicles to reduce fire risk. If it is safe and the vehicles are drivable, move them out of the traffic lanes to prevent additional collisions.

question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases under which condition?
options: a:On wet or icy roads,b:On dry paved highways,c:During daylight only
note: Stopping distance increases when traction is reduced, such as on wet, icy, snowy, or loose gravel roads. Because your tires cannot grip the road as well, it takes more time and distance to stop, so you must slow down and leave a larger following gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle uses its lights or siren and approaches, what must a driver do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Speed up and stay in lane.,c:Ignore and continue driving normally.,d:Pull to the left and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' sign means:
options: a:That the new 35 mph speed limit begins at the next speed limit sign.,b:That you have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.,c:That the new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.
note: A reduced speed sign means the new lower speed limit begins at that sign. You should already be slowing so that by the time you reach the sign, you are at or below the posted reduced speed.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check the blind spot before changing lanes called?
options: a:A bad driving habit.,b:An unnecessary action.,c:A good driving habit.,d:A mirror-only check.
note: Turning your head to quickly glance over your shoulder before changing lanes is a good driving habit. This blind-spot check lets you see areas your mirrors cannot show, helping you avoid vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that may be alongside you.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line on the highway?
options: a:At any time without checking for traffic.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:When it is safe to change lanes.,d:Only to make a U-turn.
note: Dashed (broken) white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross them to change lanes or pass, but only after checking mirrors and blind spots and making sure it is safe to move.

question: What should drivers know about large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and need more space to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They require less room to make turns.,d:They always maintain lower speeds than cars.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots on all sides and need more distance to stop and more space to turn and maneuver. Give them extra room and avoid driving alongside them where the driver may not see you.

question: What must you do at a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Drive carefully without stopping.,b:Slow down but do not stop.,c:Stop, yield, and proceed only when safe.,d:Merge to the right and continue.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red traffic signal mean?
options: a:The same thing as a stop sign.,b:The traffic signal is broken.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.,d:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.
note: A flashing red signal means the same as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop at the line or before entering the intersection, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when the way is clear.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Turn off the ignition immediately and honk.,b:Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.,c:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, move to a safe area, and stop.,d:Accelerate to reach the shoulder quickly.
note: If power steering fails, the vehicle will still steer but it will take much more effort. Keep a firm grip on the wheel, slow down, signal, and carefully steer to the side of the road or a safe place, then stop and get the problem checked.

question: What happens to tire effectiveness as speed increases on a wet roadway?
options: a:As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.,b:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,c:Water does not affect cars with good tires.
note: As speed increases on a wet roadway, your tires have less time to squeeze water out from under the tread. This reduces traction and increases the risk of hydroplaning, where your tires ride on top of the water and you can lose steering and braking control. Slowing down in wet conditions helps your tires stay in contact with the road.

question: In fog, should you use high beam headlights to improve vision?
options: a:False,b:True
note: In fog, you should not use high beams because the light reflects off the water droplets in the air and shines back at you, making it harder to see. Use low-beam headlights or fog lights instead, and reduce your speed so you have more time to react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,b:Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,c:Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop before the sidewalk or curb and yield to pedestrians and all traffic on the main road. Only proceed when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching closely enough to be a hazard.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that which light will appear next?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady green.,d:Flashing red.
note: A steady yellow traffic signal means the light is about to turn red. It warns you to prepare to stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, you should continue through with caution.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When anything makes conditions less than perfect, such as poor visibility or slippery roads.,b:Only if police direct you to.,c:Only when entering a highway.,d:Never; posted limits are always safe.
note: Posted speed limits are for ideal conditions. You must drive slower than the posted limit whenever conditions are less than perfect—such as rain, snow, ice, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility—so that you can stop safely and maintain control of your vehicle.

question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway,b:Pull out quickly to merge with traffic,c:Stop with part of your car on the roadway to warn others
note: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield the right‑of‑way to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the main road. Wait until traffic is clear and you can enter without forcing others to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without flashing signals or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
note: At a railroad crossing without active signals or gates, you must slow, look, and listen for trains and be prepared to stop. Trains always have the right‑of‑way, so you must be ready to yield and only cross when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough room to clear the tracks completely.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what is the recommended technique?
options: a:Firmly pump your brakes.,b:Lightly tap the brakes.,c:Hold down the brake pedal.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, use the "pump" or threshold braking method in an emergency stop: apply the brakes firmly to the point just before the wheels lock, then release slightly and reapply as needed. This pumping action helps you slow quickly while still being able to steer and avoid skids.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child, especially if they are in the front seat or improperly restrained.,b:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.,c:You should never place a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with an active airbag.
note: You must never place a rear‑facing infant seat in front of an active airbag because the force of the airbag can seriously injure or kill a baby. The safest place for children is properly restrained in the back seat. Always use the correct child restraint for the child’s age, size, and weight, and make sure every passenger is buckled up.

question: If a transit bus is signaling to re-enter traffic after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to alert the bus driver.,b:Yield by changing lanes or slowing to let the bus merge.,c:Speed up to pass the bus.,d:Ignore the signal and continue.
note: When a transit bus signals that it is pulling out from a stop, you should yield by slowing down or changing lanes if possible so the bus can re‑enter traffic safely. This helps traffic flow smoothly and protects passengers boarding or exiting the bus.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a center lane reserved for left turns, what maneuvers are generally permitted?
options: a:Making left turns from either direction.,b:Using the lane to pass slow-moving traffic.,c:Making U-turns at any time.,d:Driving through without turning.
note: A center left‑turn lane is for making left turns from either direction, not for passing or driving straight through. You may briefly enter it to prepare for a left turn, then complete the turn safely.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving,b:Excessive speed under the driving conditions,c:Following other vehicles too closely,d:All of the above
note: Inattentive driving, driving too fast for conditions, and following too closely are all major crash causes. Any of them can quickly lead to a collision, so all of the listed behaviors increase crash risk.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to which condition?
options: a:The effects of alcohol.,b:The effects of amphetamines.,c:The effects of anger.,d:The effects of cold medication.
note: Fatigue slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment in ways similar to alcohol. Being awake for long periods can affect driving ability about as much as having a moderate to high blood alcohol level.

question: When a crossing guard directs traffic in a school zone, how must you respond?
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,b:Copy surrounding drivers and ignore the guard.,c:Assume the guard lacks authority and continue.,d:Accelerate through the zone to clear it quickly.
note: Crossing guards have legal authority to direct traffic in school zones. You must obey their instructions just as you would a traffic signal or police officer and drive with extra caution around children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.,c:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
note: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely; if you are too close to stop safely, continue through with caution.

question: Why is it important to be especially alert to motorcycles?
options: a:They are more difficult to see than cars.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.,c:They rarely use their headlights.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and narrower than cars, so they are easier to overlook in mirrors and blind spots. Because of their size, it is also harder to judge how fast they are approaching and how far away they are. Staying especially alert helps you avoid turning or changing lanes into their path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does the term 'yield' include stopping if you cannot safely merge into traffic?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: To yield means to give the right‑of‑way to other traffic. If you are required to yield and there is not a large enough gap to merge safely, you must slow or stop and wait until it is safe to enter. You are not required to stop if you can merge safely without interfering with other traffic.

question: What is the leading cause of traffic accidents in Nevada?
options: a:Speeding.,b:Failure to yield the right-of-way.,c:Tailgating.
note: Failure to yield the right‑of‑way is one of the leading causes of crashes in many states, including Nevada. Crashes often happen when drivers turn left without yielding, pull out from side streets or driveways, or enter intersections without letting other traffic or pedestrians go first when required. Knowing and following right‑of‑way rules greatly reduces your risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection where a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a signal, who must yield?
options: a:The pedestrian.,b:Whoever started moving last.,c:The faster party.,d:The driver turning must yield.
note: When turning at an intersection, you must yield to pedestrians who are crossing the street you are turning into, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked and even if there is no signal. Pedestrians in the crosswalk have the right‑of‑way, so the turning driver must wait until they have safely crossed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.,b:Go to the next exit.,c:Make a U-turn through the median.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, stay calm, continue driving to the next exit, and then re‑enter the freeway going the opposite direction if needed. Never stop in a travel lane, back up on the freeway, or use the median or shoulder to turn around, as these actions are extremely dangerous and usually illegal.

question: Should drivers keep a safe operating distance when near a cyclist?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Drivers must give cyclists extra space because bicycles can wobble, need room to avoid road hazards, and are more vulnerable in a collision. Keeping a safe following and passing distance helps prevent sideswipes and rear‑end crashes.

question: What is the effect of consuming alcohol while taking drugs?
options: a:It has no added risk beyond alcohol alone.,b:It cures the illness the drug treats.,c:It reduces the effects of alcohol.,d:It can increase the effects of both substances and further impair driving.
note: Alcohol and many drugs both slow your brain and body. When taken together, their effects can combine or multiply, making you much more impaired than with either one alone and greatly increasing your crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While driving uphill approaching a heavy truck, what should you be aware of?
options: a:You may legally pass at any time on the hill.,b:You can always safely pass the truck on the hill.,c:The truck will speed up to maintain pace.,d:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
note: Heavy trucks often lose speed on upgrades because of their weight. Expect them to travel below the posted speed limit on hills and be cautious about passing, especially where your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

question: Which is NOT a factor in the distance required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Braking distance.,b:Perception time.,c:Reaction distance.,d:Steering ability.
note: Total stopping distance is made up of perception distance (seeing the hazard), reaction distance (moving your foot to the brake), and braking distance (the car slowing to a stop). Steering ability does not change how far it takes to stop in a straight line.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers do?
options: a:Signal and slow, watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound their horn to warn others.,c:Swing right within their lane before the turn.,d:Accelerate to clear the turn quickly.
note: To turn left safely, signal well in advance, slow down smoothly, and move into the proper lane. Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians in the crosswalk, and only turn when the path is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Proceed slowly through the intersection.,b:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,c:Stop and then proceed when clear even if the arrow is red.,d:Yield only to pedestrians then go.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and stay stopped in the direction of the arrow. You may not turn or go in that direction until the signal changes to green or a green arrow, unless a sign or officer specifically directs otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are out due to a power outage, how should drivers proceed?
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop, yielding appropriately,b:Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping,c:Park and wait for power to be restored
note: When a traffic signal is completely dark due to a power outage, treat the intersection like a four‑way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed in turn: first to stop goes first, and yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in or clearly entering the intersection.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means:
options: a:Pass through at normal speed,b:Stop and wait for a green light,c:Slow down and proceed with caution
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed with extra caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield and react to other traffic, pedestrians, or hazards in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a roundabout, you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Slow down as you approach.
note: When approaching a roundabout, reduce your speed and be prepared to yield to traffic already in the circle and to pedestrians in crosswalks. Enter only when there is a safe gap, and travel through the roundabout at low speed.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Railroad crossings.,c:School zones.,d:Stop ahead.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing. It means you must look and listen for trains and yield the right‑of‑way to any approaching train, stopping if necessary before the tracks.

question: What causes 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Frequent rest stops.,b:Too much sleep the night before a trip.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods without active scanning.,d:Listening to loud music.
