note: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead for long periods without actively scanning mirrors, instruments, and the road environment. Your mind drifts, you become less alert, and your reaction time slows, even though your eyes are technically open.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving at the same speed.
note: When a tire blows out, the sudden change in traction can cause you to lose control. Hold the steering wheel firmly, stay off the brakes at first, and gently ease off the accelerator so the vehicle slows gradually. Once it is stable and under control, brake lightly if needed and steer to a safe place off the road.

question: If your wheels slip off the pavement edge, what is the safest recovery method?
options: a:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.,b:Grip the wheel, slow gradually, then steer back onto the pavement when safe.,c:Slam on your brakes and stop.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, a sudden jerk of the steering wheel or hard braking can cause you to skid or lose control. Keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator to slow gradually, and when your speed is under control and traffic allows, steer smoothly back onto the pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is failure to yield the right-of-way a leading cause of accidents in Nevada?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Failure to yield the right-of-way is one of the leading causes of crashes in Nevada and many other states. Not yielding when required—such as at intersections, when turning left, or when entering a roadway—creates conflicts with other vehicles and increases the risk of serious collisions.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It has no effect on driving ability.,b:It makes you less likely to have an accident.,c:It lowers your ability to concentrate on driving.,d:It improves focus and reaction.
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you, narrow your attention, and slow your reactions. When you are upset, angry, or very worried, it is harder to concentrate on traffic, signs, and hazards, which increases your crash risk. It is safer to drive only when you are calm and focused.

question: A curb painted which color designates a reserved handicap parking space?
options: a:Blue,b:White,c:Yellow
note: Blue-painted curbs or markings indicate parking spaces reserved for vehicles displaying a valid disabled/handicapped plate or placard. Parking there without proper authorization is illegal and may result in fines and towing.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke affect driving?
options: a:Are distracting activities.,b:Do not affect driving abilities.,c:Help maintain driver alertness.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction because it takes at least one hand off the wheel and can draw your eyes and attention away from the road. Any activity that interferes with full control of the vehicle or focus on driving increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already within an intersection and the light turns yellow, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection.,b:Signal and turn around.,c:Back up to avoid entering the intersection.,d:You should continue carefully through the intersection.
note: If the light turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection, continue through carefully and clear the intersection. Do not stop suddenly in the intersection, back up, or try to turn around. The yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red for traffic that has not yet entered.

question: For drivers 21 and older, what minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes it illegal to drive?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.08 percent.,d:0.10 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older in most U.S. states, including Nevada, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Even at lower levels, alcohol can impair judgment and reaction time, so you should never drive after drinking.

question: What is a safe technique for driving through a curve?
options: a:Slow down as you enter and accelerate as you exit.,b:Maintain the same speed through the entire curve.,c:Speed up as you enter and slow down as you exit.
note: Before entering a curve, slow down to a safe speed while the vehicle is still straight, then steer smoothly through the curve and gently accelerate as you exit. Braking hard in the curve can cause loss of traction and control.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Do not enter the street or crosswalk if vehicles are approaching,b:Always insist you have the right-of-way over vehicles,c:Enter any time because drivers must stop
note: Pedestrians should not step into the street or crosswalk if vehicles are close enough to be a hazard. Even if you may have the legal right‑of‑way, a driver might not see you or be able to stop in time. Wait until it is clearly safe and traffic has stopped or there is enough distance for vehicles to yield.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase your following distance,b:Speed up to get off the road quickly,c:Ignore it and maintain normal distance
note: When it starts to sleet or snow, roads become slippery and stopping distances increase. You should clear your windshield and mirrors for maximum visibility and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react and stop smoothly.

question: How should you behave at a school crossing sign?
options: a:Always stop, whether there’s a stop sign or not.,b:Always sound your horn when you see children.,c:Watch for children and be ready to stop.
note: A school crossing sign warns you that children may be crossing the road. You must slow down, watch carefully for children, and be ready to stop. Always yield to pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk, but you are not required to stop if no children or pedestrians are present and there is no stop control.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, look and be ready to stop,b:Stop immediately in all cases,c:Drive faster to clear the tracks quickly
note: As you approach a railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If warning lights are flashing, gates are down, or a train is clearly approaching, you must stop before the tracks—typically 15 to 50 feet away—and remain stopped until it is safe to proceed.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Only when parallel parking,b:Only when reversing,c:Before changing lanes or turning and when pulling toward or away from a curb
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Before changing lanes, turning, or pulling toward or away from a curb, quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure no vehicle, cyclist, or pedestrian is hidden in your blind spot.

question: Before starting the ignition, what should you do regarding seat belts?
options: a:Buckle your seat belt and ensure all passengers are buckled.,b:Buckle only the adult passengers.,c:Ensure only children are buckled first.,d:Start the car then buckle everyone as you drive.
note: You should always buckle your own seat belt before starting the car and make sure every passenger is properly restrained. The driver is responsible for ensuring that all required occupants, especially children, are using seat belts or appropriate child restraints before the vehicle moves.

question: Are drivers required to stop for a school bus when its red lights are flashing?
options: a:True: Yes, drivers must stop.,b:False: Drivers may pass carefully.,c:Only on two-lane roads.,d:Only if children are visible.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, drivers must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. The main exception is on a divided highway with a physical median, where oncoming traffic on the opposite side usually does not have to stop.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Overcorrect with sharp steering.,b:Steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go and remain calm.,c:Turn into oncoming traffic.,d:Brake hard immediately.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This is often described as steering in the direction of the skid. Avoid hard braking and sudden steering inputs, which can make the skid worse.

question: What are the driving risks associated with worn or bald tires?
options: a:Can make turning and handling more difficult.,b:Are more likely to hydroplane on wet roads.,c:Can increase your stopping distance.,d:All of the above.
note: Worn or bald tires greatly reduce traction. This increases your stopping distance, makes it harder to turn or handle the vehicle, and raises the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads. Keeping tires in good condition is essential for safe braking and steering control.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and then driving?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.,d:Safe as long as you feel okay to drive.
note: Drinking alcohol and then driving is a serious traffic safety problem. Even small amounts of alcohol slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, and impair judgment, greatly increasing your risk of a crash and of harming yourself and others.

question: Is it ever appropriate to drive as slowly as 10 mph?
options: a:True — some conditions may require driving as slowly as 10 mph,b:False — 10 mph is always too slow,c:Only in school zones
note: You must always adjust your speed to match road, weather, and traffic conditions, even if that means driving far below the posted speed limit. In very hazardous situations—such as ice, heavy fog, or severe congestion—it can be appropriate and safer to drive as slowly as 10 mph, as long as you are not creating an unreasonable hazard for other traffic.

question: On a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when may you cross them?
options: a:Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross these lines to pass other vehicles, but only if there is no oncoming traffic.,c:Cross these lines under no circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean you must not cross them to pass. However, you may carefully cross double solid yellow lines to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, alley, or private road when it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a steady green traffic light, what should drivers do?
options: a:Proceed but yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection,b:Stop regardless of the traffic,c:Treat it as a four-way stop
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is not prohibited, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles still in the intersection. You should approach at a speed that allows you to stop safely if the light changes to yellow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When using a roundabout, what should you do before entering?
options: a:Drive in a clockwise direction.,b:Yield to entering traffic.,c:Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
note: Traffic in a roundabout moves counterclockwise. Before entering, you must slow down and yield to all traffic already in the roundabout, as well as to pedestrians in crosswalks. Enter only when there is a safe gap; do not stop inside the roundabout to yield to entering traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing other vehicles is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:Only when police are present.,b:Only at night.,c:Only on one-way streets.,d:At intersections, on hills, curves, and railroad crossings.
note: Passing is especially dangerous and often illegal at intersections, on hills and curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, and at or near railroad crossings. In these areas, your view of oncoming traffic or crossing hazards is limited, so you must not move into the opposing lane to pass.

question: A pedestrian begins to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Flash your headlights to warn the pedestrian.,b:Slow down and be ready to stop, yielding to the pedestrian.,c:Speed up and pass in front of them.,d:Honk and proceed if the pedestrian hesitates.
note: You must always be prepared to slow or stop for pedestrians. Drivers are required to yield the right‑of‑way to pedestrians in crosswalks and when they are already crossing your path, even if the crosswalk is unmarked. Do not try to scare, rush, or signal them with your horn or headlights; simply slow, yield, and stop if needed.

question: Where is a motorcycle operator allowed to use a full traffic lane?
options: a:Only on city streets,b:Only on rural highways,c:On any highway or street where motorcycles are permitted,d:On freeways only
note: A motorcycle is entitled to use a full traffic lane, just like any other motor vehicle, on any road where motorcycles are allowed. Other drivers must not crowd a motorcycle or share its lane. In many states, two motorcycles may ride side‑by‑side in a single lane, but a car may not share that lane with them.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When following a large vehicle that blocks your vision or in conditions like bad weather, heavy traffic, or being tailgated.,b:Only in city traffic.,c:Only when exiting an expressway.,d:Never, keep a constant distance.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever conditions make it harder to see, stop, or react in time. This includes following large vehicles that block your view, driving in bad weather, at higher speeds, in heavy traffic, at night, or when you are being tailgated. More space gives you extra time to avoid sudden hazards.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, what must you do?
options: a:Make every effort to give it a clear path of travel by safely moving to the right and stopping.,b:Speed up to avoid it.,c:Stop in the lane where you are and block it.,d:Ignore it if it is in the oncoming lanes.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and/or siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by officials. Do not speed up, race, or block the vehicle’s path; your goal is to give it a clear, safe route through traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a right turn, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:Close to the right curb or edge of the street, observing any bike or turn lanes.,d:In any lane, position does not matter.
note: For a right turn, you should position your vehicle as close to the right curb or edge of the roadway as is safe, while respecting any bike lanes or right‑turn‑only lanes. Being properly positioned reduces the chance of cutting across other lanes and helps other drivers and cyclists predict your movement.

question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean?
options: a:You must stop and then proceed when the light turns circular green.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular green, but you must turn in the arrow's direction.,c:It applies only on one-way streets.,d:It allows any direction of travel from the lane.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow. Traffic with a green arrow may proceed only in the direction the arrow points, and oncoming traffic and conflicting pedestrians are usually stopped by a red light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following takes precedence over the others?
options: a:A steady red light.,b:A stop sign.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A police officer directing traffic.
note: Instructions from a police officer or other authorized traffic officer always override traffic lights, signs, and pavement markings. You must follow the officer’s directions even if they conflict with the normal traffic control devices.

question: Before changing lanes, what sequence should you perform?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles.,b:Check your side view mirror.,c:Check your rearview mirror.,d:Check your rearview mirror, then your side mirror, then quickly turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, use the full sequence: check your rearview mirror to see traffic behind you, check your side mirror for traffic in the lane you want to enter, then quickly turn your head to check your blind spot. Only when the lane is clear should you move over.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and blinds you, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.,b:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.,c:Look toward the right side of the road until the car passes.
note: When an oncoming vehicle’s high beams blind you, do not look directly at the lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide until the vehicle passes.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?
options: a:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
note: Heavy trucks and other large vehicles need more distance to stop because of their size and weight. When driving near them, avoid cutting in front of them and give them extra space so they have enough room to slow or stop safely.

question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?
options: a:Turn your radio down so you can hear an approaching train.,b:Stop at least 50 feet from the tracks and open your door to listen.,c:Wait for a flagger to tell you when to cross.,d:Approach cautiously and cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction.
note: At passive railroad crossings that only have a crossbuck and no lights or gates, you must slow down, look, and listen carefully for trains in both directions. Be prepared to stop, and only proceed when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to fully clear the tracks. If a flagger is present, you must obey their directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which steps should you take?
options: a:Signal only if traffic is present, then change lanes.,b:Turn your head quickly without signaling.,c:Signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,d:Check the blind spot only if you hear a horn.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal in advance to let other drivers know your intentions, then check your mirrors and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move into the new lane when it is clear and safe. Never rely solely on mirrors or on hearing a horn.

question: What lane width are motorcycles entitled to on the road?
options: a:Half the width of a lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:The bicycle lane only.,d:Only the right edge of the lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other motor vehicle. Other drivers should not crowd them or share the lane side‑by‑side. Give motorcycles the same space and respect you would give a car.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:Drive carefully and proceed through the intersection with caution.,b:Stop and wait for the light to change.,c:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed with extra caution. Look for cross traffic, pedestrians, and any hazards before entering the intersection, and be prepared to yield if necessary.

question: When driving in fog, should you use your low-beam headlights?
options: a:TRUE: Use low-beam headlights in fog.,b:FALSE: Use high beams in fog.,c:Use parking lights only.,d:Use four-way flashers instead.
note: In fog, always use low‑beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help other drivers see you without increasing glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to use a shared center turn lane?
options: a:As a travel lane to pass other vehicles.,b:To make a left turn onto another street, road, or driveway.,c:To make a right turn onto another street or highway.
note: A shared center turn lane is reserved for vehicles making left turns from either direction. You may use it to turn left onto another street, road, or driveway, or to wait to turn left from a side street or driveway onto the main road. It must not be used as a through lane or for passing other vehicles.

question: If a train is near enough to be dangerous, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk.
note: If a train is close enough to be a hazard, you must stop and wait. Do not cross until the train has completely passed, any additional tracks are clear, and warning devices (lights, bells, gates) have stopped operating. Trains cannot stop quickly, so you must stay off the tracks whenever there is any risk.

question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Slow down to provide space in front of your vehicle for them to pass safely.,c:Maintain exact speed so they cannot pass.,d:Change lanes immediately regardless of traffic.
note: When another driver is passing you, help them do it safely. Slightly reduce your speed to create more space in front of your vehicle so the passing driver has a safe gap to move back into the lane. Never speed up to block a pass, and only change lanes if it is safe and actually needed.

question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Nighttime is not the safest time for cyclists. Even with lights and reflectors, cyclists are harder for drivers to see in the dark, and judging distance and speed is more difficult. Both cyclists and drivers must use extra caution at night, with cyclists using proper lighting and reflective gear and drivers scanning carefully.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how dangerous is driving at night?
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:No different.,c:More dangerous.,d:Only more dangerous on rural roads.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous than daytime driving. Your visibility is reduced, headlights limit how far ahead you can see, and glare from other vehicles can affect your vision. In addition, there are often more fatigued or impaired drivers on the road at night, increasing overall risk.

question: What should you do first when your visibility is reduced?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: When visibility drops because of fog, heavy rain, or darkness, your first response should be to slow down. Lower speed gives you more time to see hazards and react safely. Then, as needed, turn on your low‑beam headlights and windshield wipers so you can see and be seen.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Continue driving, as you have the right-of-way.,c:Stop completely and proceed when safe.
note: A flashing red light must be treated the same as a stop sign. You are required to come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then look in all directions and proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: When a curb is painted red, what does it generally indicate?
options: a:Loading zones only.,b:Only handicap parking is allowed.,c:Drivers may park for a limited time.,d:No stopping, standing, or parking at any time.
note: Red-painted curbs generally mean no stopping, standing, or parking at any time. This is used in areas where vehicles must stay clear, such as near fire hydrants, bus zones, or intersections, except where specific signs allow brief stops for buses or other authorized vehicles.

question: When backing, what is the proper technique?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Back quickly to minimize time spent reversing.,c:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.,d:Open your door while reversing.
note: When backing, you should turn your head and look directly through the rear window while moving slowly. Mirrors and cameras can help, but they have blind spots. Physically turning to look behind you gives the best view of pedestrians, children, and obstacles.

question: What is one primary effect of alcohol on driving ability?
options: a:Puts you to sleep.,b:Wakes you up.,c:Slows reflexes and reaction time.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the brain and nervous system. This reduces your reflexes and reaction time and impairs judgment, making it harder to respond quickly to traffic, signals, and unexpected hazards, even if you do not feel very drunk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light has the same meaning as which sign?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A speed limit sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must make a full stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane,b:When it requires driving off the pavement,c:On a narrow bridge
note: You may pass on the right only when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a clearly marked lane or enough paved roadway to do so safely without leaving the pavement. You must never pass on the right by driving off the roadway.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who doesn't obey traffic laws?
options: a:Is in the right because bicyclists don’t have to obey traffic laws.,b:Can be ticketed.,c:Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. They must obey traffic signals, signs, and lane markings, and they can receive tickets for violations just like motorists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a stop is required at an intersection but no stop line or crosswalk is marked, what should a driver do?
options: a:Is not required to stop.,b:Slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.,c:Stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.
note: When you must stop at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic. Do not move into the intersection to get a better view; remain stopped where you can see while still outside the intersection.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:Only if you are in a hurry.,b:When the train has fully passed and gates are raised.,c:Under no circumstances.,d:If the lights have stopped flashing but gates are still down.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates. Stay stopped until the train has passed, the warning devices stop, and the gates are fully raised before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against a red signal. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,b:Honk your horn.,c:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
note: Even when you have a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk or intersection, even if they are crossing against their signal. Stopping and allowing them to cross is the safest and legally required action to prevent a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to exceed the speed limit while passing another vehicle?
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:Yes, if you pass quickly.,c:Only on multi-lane highways.,d:No, exceeding the posted speed limit is always unlawful.
note: Posted speed limits apply at all times, including when you are passing another vehicle. You must complete any passing maneuver without exceeding the speed limit, using good judgment and only passing where it is legal and safe to do so.

question: How can you avoid a truck or bus blind spot?
options: a:Never pass them.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.,c:Flash your lights at them.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along both sides and directly behind them. To stay visible and safe, avoid driving right alongside them for long periods and never follow too closely. Pass promptly and give them extra space.

question: When a curb is painted green, what does it normally indicate?
options: a:Drivers may park for a limited time.,b:No stopping at any time.,c:Handicapped parking only.,d:Loading and unloading only.
note: A green-painted curb typically means you may stop or park for a limited time, as indicated by nearby signs or markings. It is intended for short-term parking, so you must obey the posted time limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop simultaneously, who yields?
options: a:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,c:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
note: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right-of-way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions at intersections.

question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed.,c:Passing is allowed if you are at the top a hill.
note: Two solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean traffic in both directions must not cross the lines to pass. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road, or when specifically allowed by law (such as when directed by a police officer).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, you arrive simultaneously with a vehicle on your right. Who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You, because you were following traffic signs.,b:The vehicle on your right.,c:Whoever signals first.,d:You if you are turning left.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no traffic controls.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what is the proper action?
options: a:Use any speed and merge quickly.,b:Signal, accelerate to match traffic speed, and merge into a gap.,c:Stop at the ramp end and wait for a large gap.,d:Merge slowly below highway speed to be cautious.
note: When entering a highway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge into a suitable gap. Stopping at the end of the ramp or merging much slower than traffic can be dangerous.

question: What is the best response to a tailgater?
options: a:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,b:Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
note: If someone is following too closely, avoid sudden braking or speeding up. Instead, if possible, change lanes or gradually slow down so the tailgater can pass. This increases your following distance ahead and reduces the chance of a rear‑end collision.

question: Which action most reduces the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Use tires with proper air pressure.,b:Do not speed when the roads are wet.,c:Replace tires with bad tread.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. The faster you drive on wet roads, the more likely you are to hydroplane. Keeping your speed down in wet conditions is the most effective way to reduce this risk, along with maintaining proper tire pressure and good tread.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This helps avoid confusion and collisions by giving a clear rule for who goes first.

question: When a traffic signal displays a flashing yellow arrow for left turns, what may drivers do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before turning.,b:Merge immediately without yielding.,c:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow for a left turn means you are allowed to turn left, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and any pedestrians in the crosswalk. Only turn when the way is clear; it is not a protected turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multi-lane road with a 'Merging traffic' sign, what is the appropriate response?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles; move over if no one is beside you.,b:Always remain at your current speed regardless of merging traffic.,c:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.,d:Speed up to prevent merging vehicles from entering.
note: When you see a merging traffic sign, you should be prepared to let vehicles enter your lane. If it is safe and there is no vehicle beside you, move over to create space. If you cannot move over, adjust your speed to allow merging traffic to enter smoothly.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what is the immediate correct action?
options: a:Reach down and try to pull up the pedal.,b:Turn off the ignition while driving fast.,c:Shift into neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake while keeping eyes on the road.,d:Shift to park to stop the engine.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift the transmission into neutral, and apply steady pressure on the brakes. Steer to a safe place off the road, then once you are stopped, turn off the engine. Do not turn off the ignition while moving at high speed or shift into park, as this can cause loss of control.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey a specified instruction are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs,b:Information signs,c:Warning signs
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do or must not do, such as speed limits, stop signs, yield signs, and no-turn signs. These signs are legally enforceable and must be obeyed.

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a:Octagon (eight-sided).,b:Rectangle.,c:Circle.,d:Triangle.
note: A stop sign is always an octagon (eight-sided). This unique shape helps drivers recognize it quickly, even if visibility is poor or the sign is partially blocked, and it always means you must come to a complete stop.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the train.,b:Stop if a train is nearby and never go around lowered gates.,c:Look for a detour to bypass the crossing.,d:Cross quickly without slowing.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching tracks and must be ready to slow or stop. If a train is coming or the gates are down, you must stop and never drive around lowered gates or ignore flashing lights or bells.

question: When driving in fog, should you use high beams?
options: a:False,b:True
note: In fog, you should not use high beams because the light reflects off the water droplets and creates glare, making it harder to see. Use low beams or fog lights so the light stays lower on the road and improves visibility.

question: Does increasing your speed increase your stopping distance?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: As speed increases, you travel farther during your reaction time and your brakes need more distance to stop the vehicle. This means total stopping distance (perception + reaction + braking) becomes much longer at higher speeds.

question: What is the only reliable way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.,d:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows your body to process and eliminate alcohol from your system. Coffee, cold showers, or exercise might make you feel more awake, but they do not lower your BAC or make you safe to drive.

question: How should you position your vehicle relative to a motorcycle on the road?
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,b:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,c:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other motor vehicle. You should never try to share the same lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle or drive on the shoulder next to one. Give them the entire lane and plenty of space.

question: If you are stopped by a police officer, what should you do while waiting for the officer to approach?
options: a:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.,b:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
note: During a traffic stop, stay in your vehicle unless the officer instructs otherwise, keep your hands visible on the steering wheel, and wait for directions before reaching for documents. This helps keep everyone safe and avoids sudden movements that could concern the officer.

question: Are you allowed to text while driving?
options: a:If you are very skilled drivers.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:At any time in any manner.
note: Using a handheld device to send or read non-voice communications (including texting) while driving is prohibited.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted (one hand on wheel, talking), what should you do?
options: a:Avoid following the driver's example.,b:Give the vehicle extra space.,c:Know that the driver in the vehicle ahead is reducing their safety margin by being an inattentive driver.
note: A distracted driver is more likely to make sudden or unpredictable moves. To protect yourself, increase your following distance and give that vehicle extra space. This larger gap gives you more time to react if the distracted driver brakes suddenly, drifts, or makes an unexpected maneuver.

question: Which is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Parking perfectly in marked spots.,b:Always using turn signals.,c:Driving exactly at the speed limit.,d:Weaving between lanes.
note: Weaving between lanes, drifting, or making sudden, erratic movements are common signs of an impaired driver. If you see this behavior, stay well back, avoid trying to pass, and if safe to do so, report the vehicle to authorities with its location and description.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your plans.,b:Just after you start to pass.,c:Only if asked by other drivers.,d:Never; passing requires no signal.
note: Before passing or changing lanes, you must signal early enough for other drivers to see and react to your intentions. Signaling only as you start to pass does not give others enough warning and can lead to unsafe situations.

question: If you see or hear an emergency vehicle while on a divided multilane highway, how should you respond?
options: a:Disregard the signal if there are other lanes available for the emergency vehicle.,b:Slow down, move as far to the right as you safely can, and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.,c:Stop immediately in your lane without moving over.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights or siren is approaching, you must yield the right-of-way by moving as far as you safely can to the right and stopping until it has passed. On a divided multilane highway, you still must slow, move over, and stop if the vehicle is approaching from behind or ahead in your side of the roadway.

question: At night when another vehicle is approaching, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:No lights if the street is lit.,b:High beams.,c:Parking lights only.,d:Low beams.
note: At night, you must dim your headlights to low beams when an oncoming vehicle is within a reasonable distance so you do not blind the other driver. High beams are for open, unlit roads when no traffic is close in front of you or approaching.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which sign?
options: a:Solid red light.,b:Yield sign.,c:Stop sign.,d:School zone sign.
note: A flashing red traffic light means the same as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,c:Slow down until it passes you.
note: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an approaching emergency vehicle, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as you safely can and stopping until the vehicle has passed.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams, where should you look?
options: a:The center of the road.,b:Either side of the road at random.,c:The right side of the road.,d:Directly into the bright lights to gauge intensity.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly into the glare because it can temporarily blind you. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide while still keeping general awareness of the roadway. This helps you maintain your lane position and see enough of the road until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp should:
options: a:Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Has the right-of-way.,c:May force their way into traffic.
note: When entering an interstate or freeway from an entrance ramp, you must use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and then merge only when there is a safe gap. Drivers already on the interstate have the right-of-way, so you must yield to them and adjust your speed or wait until it is safe to merge.

question: How close to a railroad crossing may you legally park?
options: a:100 feet,b:75 feet,c:50 feet
note: You must not park within 50 feet of the nearest rail at a railroad crossing. Keeping this distance helps ensure that trains and other drivers have a clear view of the tracks and that your vehicle does not block warning devices or create a hazard near the crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, which scan pattern should you use before moving forward?
options: a:Look left first, then right, then left again.,b:Check only the vehicle ahead then go.,c:Look left only because those vehicles are closer.,d:Look in the mirrors and proceed immediately.
note: Before moving from a stop sign, first look left, then right, then left again. Traffic from the left is closer to you and will reach the intersection sooner, so you must check that direction first. After checking right, a final look left confirms it is still clear before you enter the intersection. Also check for pedestrians, cyclists, and any vehicles that may be turning.

question: When driving in an area where children may be present, what should you expect?
options: a:To know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:To stop at the curb before crossing the street.,c:They may run out in front of you without looking.
note: In areas where children may be present—such as schools, parks, and residential neighborhoods—you should expect that children may suddenly run into the street without looking. Drive slowly, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop at any time because children are less predictable and may not judge traffic safely.

question: Which of these will help reverse the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Hot coffee.,b:Time.,c:Fresh air.
note: Only time reduces your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize alcohol at its own slow rate; coffee, cold showers, or fresh air may make you feel more awake but do not make you less impaired or safer to drive.

question: While driving on major highways, you should:
options: a:Stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and be ready to react to hazards,b:Stare straight ahead to avoid distraction,c:Relax and let cruise control handle everything
note: On highways you must stay alert, scan ahead, check mirrors frequently, and be ready to react to hazards. Staring straight ahead narrows your field of vision, and relying on cruise control alone can make you less attentive and slower to respond.

question: What is a vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:An area you cannot see in your mirrors and must turn your head to check.,b:The area directly behind your vehicle.,c:What you see in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors and cannot see without turning your head. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly glance over your shoulder to check these areas so you do not move into a space already occupied by another vehicle.

question: Orange work zone signs indicate:
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and construction activity ahead,b:The start of a school zone,c:A hospital nearby
note: Orange signs are used for construction and maintenance work zones. They warn you of roadwork, lane shifts, workers, and equipment ahead, so you should slow down, be prepared for sudden stops, and follow posted directions.

question: May you use only parking lights while driving at night?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Driving at night with only parking lights is unsafe and illegal. When it is dark or visibility is reduced, you must use your headlights so other drivers can see you and you can see the road clearly.

question: True or false: A railroad crossbuck sign should be treated like a yield sign.
options: a:Only with lights flashing,b:False,c:Only at night,d:True
note: A railroad crossbuck is treated like a yield sign. You must slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If a train is approaching, you must yield the right‑of‑way and wait until it has completely cleared the crossing and it is safe before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:During daylight hours only.,b:At any time for passing.,c:When following a large vehicle.,d:Only to make a turn into or out of a driveway, alley, or side road when safe.
note: A solid yellow center line generally means you must not cross it to pass another vehicle. However, you may cross a solid yellow line when it is safe and legal to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, alley, or side road. Always yield to oncoming traffic and complete the turn without interfering with other road users.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks open, what is the safest procedure?
options: a:Blow your horn.,b:Slam on your brakes.,c:Shift to neutral, brake smoothly, steer to a safe area, then turn off the ignition once stopped.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep control of the vehicle first. Shift to neutral, apply the brakes smoothly, and steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place. Once you are safely off the road and stopped, then turn off the ignition. Turning the key too early can lock the steering or disable power steering and brakes, making it harder to control the car.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked on the side of the road, what should you assume?
options: a:Assume that the driver will open the car door as you approach.,b:Speed up.,c:Slam on your brakes.
note: When passing a parked vehicle, you should expect that someone might open a door or step out suddenly. Slow down if needed, leave extra space, and be ready to stop or steer around an opening door. Assuming the door may open keeps you prepared and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: When approaching an unprotected railroad crossing without signals, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to cross before a train arrives.,b:Always come to a full stop regardless of visibility.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop if a train is near.,d:Assume there is always a signal at every crossing.
note: At an unprotected railroad crossing with no lights or gates, slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Be prepared to stop if a train is near or if you cannot see clearly down the tracks. Never try to beat a train; trains are much faster and closer than they may appear and always have the right‑of‑way.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if the bus is stopped on the shoulder and empty.,b:Only if students are in the roadway.,c:If the bus is stopped with red lights flashing to load or unload children.,d:Never if you are in the opposing lane.
note: On a two-lane road, all drivers in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and is loading or unloading children. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII charges?
options: a:Alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some prescription/OTC medicines,b:Only beer and wine,c:Only illegal drugs
note: Driving can be impaired by many substances, not just alcohol. Illegal drugs, inhalants, and even some prescription or over‑the‑counter medicines can slow your reactions, affect judgment, and make it unsafe to drive. If a substance affects your ability to drive safely, you can be charged with DUII regardless of whether it is legal or prescribed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When your slow driving disrupts the normal flow of traffic,b:Whenever you are in a construction zone,c:Only on rural roads
note: You are required to travel at a speed that is safe for conditions and that does not unnecessarily block or impede normal traffic. If you drive so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic when it is safe to go faster, you can be cited, even if you are below the posted speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Vehicles in the roundabout.,b:Bicyclists in the roundabout.,c:Pedestrians in the roundabout.,d:All of the above.
note: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to all traffic already in the circle, including vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in crosswalks at the entrances and exits. Enter only when there is a safe gap and continue yielding to anyone already in the roundabout.

question: What color are regulatory signs typically?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Green
note: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit, no parking, and lane use control signs, are typically white with black or red symbols or lettering. They tell you about laws and regulations you must obey while driving.

question: Which statement about sudden weather changes is correct?
options: a:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.,b:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.,c:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.,d:All of the above
note: When weather changes suddenly, you must adjust how you drive. In rain, fog, or other bad conditions, slow down, increase following distance, and be especially alert to vehicles behind you that may not slow down as quickly.

question: At a light rail crossing, drivers should always:
options: a:Look both ways before crossing and obey all signals and signs,b:Assume the train will stop for you,c:Drive around lowered gates if there's no train in sight
note: At light rail or train crossings, always look carefully in both directions and obey all warning signs, lights, and gates. Trains cannot stop quickly and do not swerve, so you must never drive around lowered gates, even if you do not see a train.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,b:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will contact the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.,b:The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.,c:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
note: Alcohol can interact with prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines in ways that increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment more than either substance alone. Because these effects can multiply and be unpredictable, you should avoid drinking when taking any medication that can cause drowsiness or affect alertness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The largest vehicle.,b:The car on the left.,c:The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Yielding to the right helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: True or False: It is safe to use cruise control when driving on snowy or icy roads as long as you reduce speed.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Cruise control should never be used on snowy or icy roads. If your tires lose traction, cruise control can cause the vehicle to accelerate or brake unexpectedly, making it harder to regain control. Always drive manually and adjust your speed to conditions on slippery roads.

question: When must you pull to the edge of the road and allow an emergency vehicle to pass?
options: a:When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or siren is approaching in your lane or an adjacent lane.,b:Only if it is directly following you in the same lane.,c:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction on any roadway.
note: You must yield to an emergency vehicle using siren and/or flashing lights by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping. This applies when the emergency vehicle is approaching from behind you or from ahead in your lane or an adjacent lane. On a divided highway with a physical barrier, you are generally not required to stop for emergency vehicles traveling on the opposite side of the barrier.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red,d:Black
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Knowing this helps you understand when passing is allowed and which side of the road you should be on.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When encountering a flashing red light at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Ignore it if there is no traffic.,b:Slow down and proceed if clear.,c:Only yield to vehicles on your left.,d:Treat it as a stop sign and come to a complete stop before proceeding.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop at the limit line or before entering the crosswalk or intersection, look for other vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What should a driver do if taking a non-prescription drug?
options: a:Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.,b:Drink alcohol instead.,c:Read the labels on the drug before driving.
note: Many over-the-counter medicines can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction time. Always read the label for driving warnings and, if you are unsure, ask a doctor or pharmacist before driving after taking the medication.

question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes to avoid driving next to the stopped vehicle.,b:Stay in your lane and maintain your speed.,c:Drive to the right and stop immediately.
note: If an emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicle is stopped with flashing lights, change lanes away from it if it is safe. If you cannot change lanes, slow down below the posted limit and give as much space as possible.

question: You begin driving as it starts to rain. What should you do?
options: a:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,c:Slow down.
note: When rain begins, oil and dirt on the road mix with water and make the surface very slippery. You should slow down to increase traction and give yourself more time to react. Turn on your headlights so others can see you, and if visibility becomes too poor, safely pull off the road and wait until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn on city streets should you signal?
options: a:20 feet,b:50 feet,c:100 feet
note: On most city streets, you should signal at least 100 feet before you turn. Signaling early gives drivers behind you, oncoming traffic, and pedestrians time to understand what you plan to do and adjust safely. Keep signaling until you complete the turn.

question: Which of the following is a correct rule about passing other vehicles?
options: a:You may not pass on a hill or in a curve.,b:You may pass another vehicle by using the shoulder of the highway.,c:Passing is allowed if your lane is next to a solid yellow line.
note: You must not pass on hills or curves where your view of oncoming traffic is limited, because you cannot be sure the opposing lane is clear. You also may not use the shoulder to pass or cross a solid yellow line to pass. Only pass where passing is permitted and you have a clear view and enough space to complete the maneuver safely.

question: How should you treat railroad crossings?
options: a:Dangerous.,b:Safe to cross since a train is unlikely.,c:Safe places to park a car.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous because trains are large, fast, and cannot stop quickly. Approach every crossing with caution: slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, and obey all warning signs, signals, and gates. Never stop or park on the tracks, and do not cross unless you are sure there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

question: Should drivers avoid driving beside large vehicles for long periods?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along both sides, especially on the right. If you stay next to them for a long time, the driver may not see you and could change lanes into your vehicle. Either slow down to fall behind or safely pass and move ahead so you remain clearly visible.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: When another driver does not dim their high beams, looking directly at the lights can temporarily blind you. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road markings or edge line as a guide. This reduces glare while still letting you track your lane position and watch for hazards.

question: If driving at 40 mph or slower, what is the minimum recommended following distance?
options: a:Two seconds,b:Three seconds,c:Four seconds
note: A three‑second following distance is a widely recommended minimum at lower speeds because it gives you more time to see and react if the vehicle ahead suddenly slows or stops. In bad weather, at night, or when following large vehicles, you should increase this distance even more to stay safe.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light instructs drivers to:
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for green.,c:Yield only to pedestrians.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed with caution. Be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other traffic already in the intersection, and only continue when it is clearly safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Use the lane of oncoming traffic (i.e., cross the centerline) only when safe and legal,b:Never cross the centerline,c:Flash your headlights as the only signal
note: On a two‑lane, two‑way road, you must move into the oncoming lane to pass a slower vehicle. Only do this where passing is legal (no solid yellow line on your side) and when you have enough clear distance to pass without interfering with oncoming traffic. Return to your lane as soon as it is safe.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Open your window.,b:Stop driving.,c:Get some coffee.
note: Drowsy driving is dangerous; the best remedy is to stop driving and rest.

question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Use alternate routes.
note: On slippery roads, such as when it is raining, snowing, or icy, your tires have less traction and it takes longer to stop. You should increase your following distance so you have more space and time to brake gently and avoid skids. Driving as if the road were dry is unsafe, and simply choosing alternate routes does not replace adjusting your speed and following distance.

question: Is it legal to park in a handicap access aisle beside a handicap parking stall?
options: a:False,b:True
note: It is illegal to park in the striped handicap access aisle next to a disabled parking space. These aisles must stay clear so people using wheelchairs, walkers, or lifts have enough room to enter and exit vehicles safely. Only the marked stall may be used by vehicles with proper disabled parking authorization, and the access aisle must remain open.

question: Does talking or texting on a cell phone while driving significantly increase crash risk?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving greatly increases crash risk because it takes your attention away from the road. Texting is especially dangerous because it involves visual, manual, and mental distraction. Even hands‑free conversations can reduce your awareness of traffic conditions, so you should avoid phone use while driving whenever possible.

question: When may you sound your horn?
options: a:To express frustration at slow drivers,b:When approaching every intersection,c:To warn others when you have lost control of your car or to avoid collisions
note: You should use your horn only to warn other road users when you are in danger or to help prevent a collision, such as when another driver is about to move into your lane or when you lose control of your vehicle. Using the horn to show anger, impatience, or for unnecessary noise is unsafe and often illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.,b:The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.,c:One driver should continue driving without stopping.
note: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive and come to a complete stop has the right-of-way and should proceed first when safe. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Always communicate with signals and proceed cautiously.

question: After being stopped by law enforcement, should a driver immediately exit the vehicle and approach the officer?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When stopped by law enforcement, you should stay in your vehicle, keep your hands visible (usually on the steering wheel), and wait for the officer’s instructions. Exiting or approaching the officer without being asked can create a safety concern and may be seen as threatening.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting in an intersection to make a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight while waiting to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind,b:Keep wheels turned left so you can complete the turn faster,c:Flash your headlights so others will let you through
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your front wheels straight. If another vehicle hits you from behind while your wheels are turned left, your car could be pushed into oncoming traffic. Keeping the wheels straight reduces this risk and lets you complete the turn safely when there is a safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:
options: a:You have the other vehicle's permission,b:There is a shoulder to use for passing,c:You can see clearly ahead and can return to your lane before oncoming traffic arrives
note: On a two-way, two-lane road, you may only pass when you have a clear view of the road ahead, there are no signs or markings prohibiting passing, and you can complete the pass and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic. Never rely on another driver’s permission or use the shoulder to pass.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach,b:The body weight of an individual,c:How much time passes between drinks.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol’s effect depends on several factors, including how much food is in your stomach, your body weight, and how much time passes between drinks. These factors influence how quickly alcohol is absorbed and eliminated, which affects your blood alcohol concentration and level of impairment.

question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles typically have:
options: a:Smaller blind spots.,b:Larger blind spots.,c:No blind spots.,d:Blind spots only in front.
note: Large vehicles such as trucks and buses have bigger blind spots than passenger cars. These blind spots are along the sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the vehicle. Because of their size and height, it is harder for the driver to see other road users in these areas, so you should avoid lingering in a large vehicle’s blind spots.

question: When there's an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Split the difference.,b:Let the car pass and then pass the bicyclist.,c:Pull onto the shoulder.
note: When you have an oncoming vehicle on your left and a bicyclist on your right, you should not try to squeeze between them. Slow down, let the oncoming car pass first, and then move over safely to give the bicyclist plenty of space when you pass. Handling one hazard at a time reduces risk and gives you more room to avoid mistakes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.
note: If you are not in the correct lane when you reach an intersection, continue straight and go to the next intersection to make your turn from the proper lane. Sudden lane changes or turning from the wrong lane can surprise other drivers and cause crashes. Plan ahead so you are in the correct lane well before the intersection.

question: If someone is injured in an accident you caused, what should you do regarding the injured person?
options: a:Move the injured person immediately away from the scene regardless of injuries.,b:Leave the injured exactly where they are and do not render assistance.,c:Avoid moving the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid if trained.,d:Wait for others to move them before offering aid.
note: After a crash, do not move an injured person unless there is immediate danger, such as fire or risk of another collision. Moving someone with possible neck, back, or internal injuries can make those injuries worse. Keep the person warm, reassure them, and provide first aid only if you are trained, while you or someone else calls emergency services.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:Only if you are not driving.,b:Never while on a public road.,c:If riding in the back of a pickup truck.
note: It is illegal to consume or possess an open alcoholic beverage while on a public road; open containers in areas accessible to driver or passengers are prohibited.

question: What does a single dashed white line separating lanes indicate?
options: a:Drivers may change lanes or pass when safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes moving in the same direction. You may change lanes or pass across this line when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling.

question: If the solid white edge line on the right slopes leftward, what does it indicate?
options: a:You are required to turn left shortly.,b:There is an intersection ahead.,c:The road ahead becomes narrower.,d:A construction area is ahead.
note: A solid white edge line marks the outer edge of the roadway. When this line angles or slopes toward the center of the road, it warns that the usable roadway is narrowing ahead, so you should be prepared for less lane width and adjust your speed and position.

question: When should you use your parking brake?
options: a:Every time you park.,b:Only when parking on an incline.,c:Only when parked in a driveway.
note: You should set the parking brake every time you park, whether on a hill or on level ground. Using the parking brake helps keep the vehicle from rolling and reduces strain on the transmission, providing an extra layer of safety.

question: When confronted by an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating them.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
note: When dealing with an aggressive driver, your goal is to avoid conflict and increase safety. Do not retaliate or engage. Instead, avoid eye contact, slow down if needed, and safely let the aggressive driver pass so you can create space between your vehicle and theirs.

question: Why is driving at night generally more difficult than during the day?
options: a:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,c:It is always raining at night.,d:Traffic laws are different at night.
note: Driving at night is harder mainly because you cannot see as far or as clearly. Headlights limit your field of vision, and hazards are harder to detect. Use proper headlights, keep your speed low enough to stop within the distance you can see, and stay alert for pedestrians, animals, and unlit obstacles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are motorists required to yield to pedestrians even if the pedestrian is walking against the traffic light?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Drivers must always exercise due care to avoid hitting pedestrians, even when the pedestrian is crossing against the light or otherwise violating the law. You should slow or stop as needed to avoid a collision. The pedestrian may be cited for failing to obey the signal, but you are still responsible for preventing a crash whenever reasonably possible.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.,d:Blue.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and usually mark the right edge of the roadway. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions or mark the left edge on divided highways and one‑way roads.

question: Does drinking coffee reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Yes, it decreases BAC.,b:No, it has no effect on BAC.,c:It cancels the effects of alcohol.,d:It dilutes alcohol in the bloodstream.
note: Coffee, cold showers, or fresh air do not lower your blood alcohol concentration. Only time allows your body to process and eliminate alcohol. You may feel more awake after coffee, but you are still impaired until your BAC naturally decreases.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers on.,b:Slow down until it passes you.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and lights on, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your way, which lane should you enter?
options: a:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.,b:Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.,c:Turn into the middle lane.
note: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your way, you must turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you are coming from. This keeps traffic predictable and reduces the chance of sideswipe collisions. After completing the turn and when it is safe, you may change lanes if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and may turn right if not prohibited and the way is clear,b:Proceed through if no other cars are present,c:Ignore it when no police officer is present
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line. In most U.S. states, you may turn right on red after stopping, but only if there is no sign prohibiting it and the way is clear of traffic, pedestrians, and cyclists.

question: Are cell phones a serious source of driver distraction?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Cell phones are a major source of distraction because they take your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, and your mind off driving. Even hands‑free use can reduce your attention. They should be avoided while driving and, if used at all, limited to true emergencies where it is safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach, what is the correct action?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Brake and stop suddenly even if it is not safe to do so.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop if you can do so safely.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and be prepared to stop before the intersection. Only continue through if you are so close that stopping safely would be difficult or unsafe; you should never speed up to beat the red.

question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving?
options: a:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,b:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or the vehicles being driven.,c:Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
note: Alcohol affects judgment, coordination, vision, and reaction time, even in small amounts. This means drivers who have been drinking do not have full control of their bodies, minds, or vehicles and are much more likely to make dangerous mistakes.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may not pass.,b:Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers may pass if it is safe and legal to do so.,c:Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers must never cross the line.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is dashed on your side and there are no signs or conditions that prohibit it, you may cross the line to pass another vehicle, but only when it is legal and safe with enough clear distance ahead.

question: Is the speed limit in Nevada school zones always 25 mph?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Nevada school zone speed limits are not always 25 mph. They are typically either 15 mph or 25 mph and you must obey the specific speed and times shown on the posted signs.

question: When sharing the road with large commercial vehicles, which should you keep in mind?
options: a:They require extra time and space to slow and stop.,b:They always drive slower than posted speeds.,c:They have small blind spots.,d:They can stop faster than passenger vehicles.
note: Large commercial vehicles are heavy and need more time and distance to slow and stop than passenger cars. They also have large blind spots, so give them extra space and signal early when changing position around them.

question: What should you do when you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as is safe and stop.,b:Proceed slowly and allow the vehicle to pass.,c:Stop immediately where you are.
