note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as is safe and stopping until it has passed. Never stop in an intersection; if you are in one, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: Your stopping distance after you brake is affected by how fast you were driving.
options: a:Only when you have good brakes,b:Only on wet roads,c:TRUE,d:FALSE
note: Stopping distance increases as your speed increases. The faster you are driving, the longer it takes to react and the farther your vehicle will travel after you apply the brakes before coming to a complete stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving vehicle.,b:Whenever there is no oncoming traffic.,c:To pass another car when traffic is clear.,d:To turn into a driveway or make a permitted left turn.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean you may not cross them to pass or change lanes. You may cross them only to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or to make another specifically permitted left turn when it is safe.

question: True or false: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane, you must yield the right-of-way.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,d:Only if a crossing guard is present
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to a blind or visually impaired pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane, whether or not they are in a marked crosswalk. Slow down or stop as needed and give them plenty of space to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection with obstructed view, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross and can make the turn safely,b:Accelerate quickly once the first lane clears,c:Start when an oncoming driver waves you through
note: When turning left across multiple lanes, do not start the turn until you can clearly see all lanes you must cross and are sure you can complete the turn without forcing others to brake or swerve. Never rely on another driver waving you through or try to “beat” traffic by accelerating blindly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway?
options: a:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.,b:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,c:Signal and enter the freeway. Freeway traffic must yield.
note: Use the freeway entrance ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed, signal early, and merge at or near the speed of traffic. Vehicles already on the freeway have the right-of-way, so you must adjust your speed and position to merge safely without forcing them to brake suddenly.

question: True or false: A 'Merging lanes' sign means drivers should be prepared to change lanes or allow other traffic into their lane.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only merge if on a freeway.,d:Only applies to trucks
note: A merging traffic or merging lanes sign warns that another lane of traffic will join your lane. Be prepared to adjust your speed, change lanes if needed, or create a gap so vehicles can merge safely. Use your mirrors and check blind spots to cooperate with merging traffic.

question: If a flagger directs traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the flagger's directions,b:Follow only the surrounding traffic's actions,c:Assume the flagger's signs are optional
note: In construction and work zones, flaggers have the same authority as traffic signals and signs. You must obey their hand signals and signs, slow down, and proceed only as directed to protect workers and other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you will turn left onto a one-way street, you should turn into which lane?
options: a:The lane closest to your previous lane,b:The right-most lane,c:Either lane at your discretion
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, you must enter the lane closest to the lane you turned from, usually the leftmost lane on the new street. This keeps traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles that may be entering other lanes.

question: Which statement about passing a motorcycle is true?
options: a:You must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle,b:It is okay to follow a motorcycle closely,c:Motorcycles are always more balanced with two riders
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other vehicle. When passing, you must move completely into the adjacent lane and pass as you would another car. Never crowd a motorcycle or share a lane with it, and avoid following too closely because motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than cars.

question: What is required when you encounter an emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:Speed up to pass it quickly.,b:Ignore it and keep driving.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and maintain your lane.,d:Yield the right-of-way and follow any instructions given over loudspeaker.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using sirens and flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop if possible, allowing it to pass. Obey any instructions given over a loudspeaker and proceed only after the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe.

question: A red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop at the stop line or before entering any crosswalk or intersection,b:Slow down and proceed with caution,c:Ignore it if no other cars are present
note: A steady red traffic signal means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, before the crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. You must remain stopped until the light turns green and it is safe to proceed, unless a sign or signal specifically allows a turn on red where permitted by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, what must you do first?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Back up slowly.
note: When the light turns green, you may proceed only after first yielding to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles still in the intersection. A green light does not guarantee that the way is clear; you must check for people and traffic before moving.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle.
note: A slow-moving vehicle must display a reflective orange triangle with a red border on the rear of the vehicle. This emblem warns other drivers that the vehicle typically travels 25 mph or less, so they should be prepared to slow down and pass only when safe.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning while driving in wet conditions?
options: a:Drive more quickly through shallow water.,b:Drive more slowly and avoid standing water.,c:Increase tire pressure above recommended levels.,d:Use cruise control to maintain constant speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. To reduce this risk, you should slow down, especially in heavy rain, and avoid driving through standing water or puddles when possible. Proper tire tread and avoiding sudden acceleration also help.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line next to your lane means:
options: a:Do not pass from your direction.,b:You may pass with caution.,c:Slow down to below the speed limit.,d:You must change lanes immediately.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must not pass other vehicles from your direction. It marks a no-passing zone, usually where visibility is limited or it would be unsafe to move into the oncoming lane.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops.,b:Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots for traffic.,c:Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before applying the brakes.
note: To help prevent rear-end collisions, you should avoid sudden stops by slowing gradually, releasing the accelerator early, and applying the brakes smoothly so drivers behind you have time to react. Always signal your turns and lane changes, and maintain a safe following distance so you don’t have to brake abruptly.

question: What does an 'End school zone' sign indicate?
options: a:The beginning of a reduced speed zone.,b:The increased possibility of encountering pedestrians.,c:End of the reduced speed school zone.
note: An 'End school zone' sign tells you that the special reduced speed limit for the school zone has ended and the regular posted speed limit for that road now applies. You should still stay alert for children and pedestrians, but the school-zone speed restriction is no longer in effect.

question: True or false: If conditions are unsafe, you may not leave a child under eight unattended in a vehicle.
options: a:Only with windows cracked,b:False,c:True,d:Only on highways
note: You must never leave a young child alone in a vehicle when conditions could endanger their health or safety, such as extreme heat or cold. A responsible person who is at least 12 years old should stay with the child to supervise and respond quickly if something goes wrong.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the curb and stop, then look to see if it is on your street,b:Keep driving until you spot it,c:Ignore the sound
note: When you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, you must still yield the right-of-way. Safely pull as close as you can to the right curb or edge of the road and stop until you are sure the emergency vehicle has passed or it is clear you are not in its path.

question: Which practice can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Only use turn signals when necessary.,b:Drive faster than posted limits.,c:Ignore posted speed limits to keep up with traffic.,d:Allow extra travel time.
note: Allowing extra travel time helps you stay calm and patient, so you are less likely to speed, tailgate, or make aggressive maneuvers. Planning ahead, obeying speed limits, and signaling properly all reduce stress and help prevent road rage situations.

question: Large trucks' blind spots can extend how far behind the vehicle?
options: a:Up to 200 feet,b:Only a few feet,c:They have no blind spots
note: Large trucks and buses have a large blind spot directly behind them that can extend up to about 200 feet. If you follow too closely, the driver may not see you, and you will have less time to react if the truck stops suddenly. Stay back far enough to be visible and to see the truck’s mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you view a driver who travels much slower than the flow of traffic?
options: a:Is always the safest driver.,b:May be hazardous and must allow others to pass if backing up traffic.,c:Should not let following cars pass.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can be dangerous because it disrupts the flow and may cause sudden lane changes or rear-end collisions. On two-lane roads, if you are backing up a line of vehicles, you are required to pull off the road where safe and let faster traffic pass.

question: The term 'No zone' refers to:
options: a:An area where radios must be turned off,b:A special reduced-speed zone,c:The blind spots around a truck or bus where the driver cannot see you
note: The term "No Zone" refers to the large blind spots around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you. These areas are directly behind, directly in front, and along the sides of the vehicle. Staying out of these zones helps the truck or bus driver see you and reduces the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When there is a stop sign but no crosswalk, where must you stop?
options: a:Before entering the intersection,b:At the stop line if present, otherwise before entering the intersection or crosswalk,c:In the middle of the intersection
note: When there is a stop sign, you must stop before entering the intersection. If there is a stop line, stop at the line. If there is a crosswalk, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no line and no crosswalk, stop at the point just before you enter the intersection so you can see cross traffic and yield the right-of-way safely.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Ensure tires have good tread and proper pressure and reduce speed in rain.,b:Drive faster to get through puddles quickly.,c:Turn off traction control.,d:Use parking lights only in rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. To reduce this risk, keep your tires properly inflated, make sure they have good tread, and slow down when roads are wet—especially in heavy rain or standing water. Higher speeds greatly increase the chance of hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal displays a red light and a green arrow simultaneously, may you turn in the arrow’s direction?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A green arrow is a protected turn signal. When you see a green arrow with a red circular light, you may turn only in the direction of the arrow, after yielding to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection. You must remain stopped for the red light for all other movements.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the best response?
options: a:Flash your vehicle's lights to let the aggressive driver know he is wrong.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Call the police immediately.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and create space by slowing down or changing lanes when it is safe. Do not retaliate or try to "teach them a lesson," as this can quickly escalate into road rage and increase the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what does this signal mean?
options: a:The driver is signaling for you to pass.,b:The driver plans to turn left.,c:The driver plans to turn right.,d:The driver plans to stop or slow down.
note: A left arm extended downward with the palm facing back is the standard hand signal for slowing or stopping. Drivers use this when their brake lights are not working or to give extra warning to traffic behind.

question: A solid red arrow displayed by a traffic signal means:
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction,b:You may turn after yielding to oncoming traffic without stopping,c:It has no legal meaning
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped if you are in the lane controlled by that arrow. You may not turn in the direction of the arrow until it turns green or is replaced by a signal that allows movement.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Only when you see a train.,b:When directed by a flagger, stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.,c:Never; always proceed unless a train is visible.,d:Only if the crossing is marked with a crossbuck.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger directs you to stop, when a stop sign is posted and requires a stop, or when flashing red lights and/or gates indicate a train is approaching. Never go around lowered gates or ignore active signals.

question: True or false: Increasing your speed is the best way to avoid losing control on wet roads.
options: a:Only on highways,b:True,c:Only with four-wheel drive,d:False
note: On wet roads, higher speeds make it easier to lose traction and hydroplane. To maintain control, you should slow down, increase following distance, and avoid sudden steering or braking.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:A lack of sleep.,c:Any medication.,d:All of the above.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, many medications (including some prescriptions and over‑the‑counter drugs), and by fatigue or lack of sleep. Any substance or condition that slows your reactions, affects your judgment, or makes you drowsy can make driving unsafe.

question: Why must drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They are harder to see and less protected than occupants of motor vehicles,b:They obey completely different traffic laws,c:They always have the right-of-way
note: Drivers must be especially alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because they are smaller, harder to see, and have little or no protection in a crash. A minor mistake that might cause a fender‑bender between cars can cause severe injury or death to these vulnerable road users, so extra scanning and caution are required.

question: Which statement about a work zone is correct?
options: a:Work zones may be moving or stationary and are marked with orange signs; drivers should slow down and pay extra attention.,b:Work zones are always stationary and use black and white signs.,c:Work zones do not require drivers to change behavior.,d:Work zones require you to stop at all times.
note: Work zones can be stationary (like a fixed construction site) or moving (such as a line‑painting or pothole‑repair crew). They are typically marked with orange warning signs, cones, and other devices. Drivers must slow down, obey posted work‑zone speed limits, and pay close attention to workers, equipment, and changing traffic patterns.

question: If you drink socially, what helps ensure a safe ride home?
options: a:Ride with a friend who has not been drinking,b:Drink coffee before driving,c:Take a cold shower before driving
note: The only safe choice after drinking is to avoid driving entirely. Riding with a sober driver, using a taxi, rideshare, or public transit keeps you from driving while impaired. Coffee, cold showers, or other “sobering up” tricks do not reduce your blood alcohol content or make you safe to drive.

question: When driving near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, how should you behave?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Proceed normally.
note: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down, yield the right‑of‑way, and be prepared to stop. Do not honk or rush through the crossing. Give the pedestrian plenty of time and space to cross safely, as they rely on sound and predictable driver behavior.

question: Where should you maintain space around your vehicle for safety?
options: a:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.,b:Only in front of the vehicle.,c:Only in back of your vehicle.,d:On all sides of your vehicle.
note: Maintaining a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle gives you time and room to react if another driver stops suddenly, drifts into your lane, or if a hazard appears. Adequate space in front, behind, and to both sides improves visibility and allows safer braking, lane changes, and evasive maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is the correct time to slow down when using a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Before you enter the exit ramp.,b:Only after exiting the ramp entirely.,c:Keep speed constant until you reach the off-ramp end.,d:After you move onto the exit ramp.
note: On freeways, keep up with the flow of traffic until you are actually on the exit ramp. Slowing down too early in the main travel lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision. Once you have moved onto the exit ramp, reduce your speed to match the posted ramp speed and any upcoming conditions.

question: What should drivers do when road conditions are bad (rain, snow, fog)?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Increase their speed to reach the destination more quickly.,c:Decrease their following distance.
note: In rain, snow, fog, or other poor conditions, your visibility and traction are reduced, so you need more time and space to react. Increasing your following distance gives you a larger safety cushion to brake gently and avoid sudden maneuvers if the vehicle ahead slows or stops unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are drivers always allowed to make U-turns in school zones?
options: a:True: U-turns are always permitted.,b:False: U-turns are restricted in school zones except when allowed.,c:Only allowed during school hours.,d:Only allowed with a police officer present.
note: U‑turns are not automatically allowed in school zones. They are generally prohibited where signs or markings forbid them, where visibility is limited, or when they could endanger children or other road users. Only make a U‑turn in or near a school zone if it is specifically permitted, clearly safe, and legal under local law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal shows a red light together with a green arrow, what does it mean?
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.,b:You may only drive straight ahead.,c:You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
note: A red light means stop for all directions except where a green arrow is shown. A green arrow allows you to proceed only in the direction of the arrow, and only if the intersection is clear and it is safe to go. All other movements controlled by the red light must remain stopped.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your driving?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Only prescription drugs.,c:Illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter medications.,d:Only alcohol combined with drugs.
note: Any drug that affects your mind or body can impair driving, including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter medicines. Some can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. You are responsible for knowing how a drug affects you and must not drive if your ability is impaired.

question: Where is it illegal to park?
options: a:On private property with permission.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a hill.,d:In a marked bicycle lane or on a crosswalk.
note: Parking is prohibited on crosswalks and in marked bicycle lanes because these areas must remain clear for pedestrians and cyclists. Even if space appears open, stopping or parking there blocks safe passage and violates traffic laws in most jurisdictions.

question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, what does that tell you?
options: a:You are on a two-way road.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:The road is under repair.
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic flows in both directions and passing is allowed when it is safe and legal to do so. Yellow lines separate opposing traffic; white lines separate traffic moving in the same direction.

question: Which of the following are effects of alcohol?
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Poor coordination.,c:Slower judgment.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol affects many driving skills at once. It reduces concentration, harms coordination needed for steering and braking, and slows and distorts judgment, making it harder to make safe decisions in traffic.

question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?
options: a:Always come to a full stop.,b:Yield—slow down and yield the right-of-way, be prepared to stop.,c:Slow down only if an emergency vehicle is present.,d:Pedestrian crossing ahead.
note: A red and white downward-pointing triangle is a yield sign. You must slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection.

question: Which describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Maintains eye contact during a conversation with a passenger while driving.,b:Only watches the vehicle ahead of their vehicle.,c:Stares at objects off the roadway or daydreams while driving.
note: An inattentive driver lets their mind or eyes drift away from the driving task, such as staring at things off the road or daydreaming. Safe drivers stay mentally engaged and continuously scan the road, mirrors, and surroundings.

question: Who should wear seat belts for maximum effectiveness?
options: a:Only the driver.,b:All occupants of the vehicle.,c:Only those in the front seats.,d:Only on long drives.
note: Seat belts protect everyone in the vehicle, not just the driver. In a crash, unbelted passengers can be thrown around inside the car or ejected, and they can also strike and seriously injure belted occupants. For maximum safety, every person in the vehicle should wear a seat belt on every trip.

question: Is it unlawful to share a lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, and other drivers should not crowd or share that lane side‑by‑side with them. A motorcycle needs space to maneuver and to avoid road hazards, and a car in the same lane can easily sideswipe or force the rider off the road.

question: Which is true about drowsy drivers?
options: a:Drinking coffee will reliably keep them alert.,b:Drowsy drivers can appear to be intoxicated and should not rely on windows or radio for alertness.,c:Opening a window solves drowsiness.,d:They always drive slower than traffic.
note: Drowsy drivers can be as impaired as drunk drivers: their reactions are slower, judgment is poor, and they may drift out of their lane. Tricks like opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee do not reliably restore alertness. The only safe solution is to rest or change drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver signals with the left arm and hand extended upward. What does this signal mean?
options: a:The driver intends to reverse.,b:The driver intends to turn left.,c:The driver intends to turn right.,d:The driver intends to stop.
note: Standard hand signals use the left arm: straight out for a left turn, bent upward for a right turn, and bent downward for slowing or stopping. A left arm and hand extended upward tells others you intend to turn right, which is important if your turn signals are not working.

question: What is the risk of taking drugs together with alcohol?
options: a:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:It lessens the effect of alcohol.,d:It neutralizes both substances.
note: Alcohol and many drugs both depress the central nervous system. When taken together, their effects often multiply, leading to much greater impairment than either alone. This greatly increases the chance of poor judgment, slow reactions, and causing a serious crash.

question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks even briefly when moving with a stream of vehicles?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must never stop on railroad tracks, even briefly. Before you cross, be sure there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks completely. If traffic is backed up, wait before the tracks until you can cross without stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an open highway, you should signal how far before a turn?
options: a:At least 100 feet (and earlier at higher speeds),b:20 feet,c:50 feet
note: On higher‑speed or open highways, you should signal well in advance so other drivers have time to see and react to your intentions. A common rule is to signal at least 100 feet before a turn, but many state manuals recommend signaling 200–300 feet ahead at highway speeds. Signaling only 20 or 50 feet before turning does not give enough warning to drivers behind you.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?
options: a:Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.,b:Stay in your car and wait for help.,c:Get out of the car and go for help.
note: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, it is usually safest to stay with your vehicle. Your car provides shelter and is easier for rescuers to see than a person on foot. Run the engine only occasionally for heat, keep a window slightly open for fresh air, and make sure the exhaust pipe is clear of snow to prevent carbon monoxide buildup.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, pull completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your emergency flashers so others can see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt fastened unless there is an immediate danger such as fire or traffic striking your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and do not cut off the other driver.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.,b:Mileage distances to locations.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.,d:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals along the roadway.

question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,b:Using only your rearview mirror.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.
note: Before merging onto a freeway, use your mirrors and then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors so you can choose a safe gap and merge smoothly.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn while being prepared to stop.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Continue at the same speed.
note: If a child appears ready to run into the street, immediately cover the brake and be prepared to stop while giving a sharp blast of your horn to warn the child and others nearby. Use the horn to alert, but your primary responsibility is to slow or stop to avoid a collision.

question: What must you do when approaching a pedestrian who uses a guide dog or white cane?
options: a:Honk so they know to clear the way.,b:Swerve quickly around them.,c:Yield the right-of-way.
note: Stop and give the blind pedestrian the right-of-way; do not honk or attempt to steer around them abruptly.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of substance?
options: a:A depressant.,b:A stimulant.,c:An antihistamine.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain activity and impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making it dangerous to drive after drinking.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect which abilities?
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and physical coordination, even if you do not feel drunk. Because driving requires quick decisions and precise control, even small amounts of alcohol can make driving unsafe.

question: When is using your horn appropriate?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When another driver makes a mistake.,c:When another vehicle is in your way and you want them to move.
note: Use your horn only to alert others to a potential collision or to warn of immediate danger. Do not use it to show anger, impatience, or to punish other drivers for mistakes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Where signs and pavement markings indicate passing is permitted and it is safe.,b:Within an intersection if no oncoming vehicles are present.,c:On a curve if you can see ahead a short distance.,d:Anywhere if you signal before passing.
note: Passing is only safe and legal where signs and pavement markings allow it and you have enough clear space to pass without speeding or cutting back in too closely. Never pass in intersections, on curves, or where your view is blocked by hills or other obstacles.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to you.,b:You must yield to pedestrians.,c:Pedestrians must yield to you.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether marked or unmarked, when pedestrians are in or approaching your lane. Always be prepared to stop for people crossing the street.

question: What does a green arrow signal require you to do?
options: a:Proceed immediately without yielding.,b:Ignore any pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,d:Yield to vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the intersection, then complete the turn.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected movement in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians already in the intersection before you complete your turn.

question: Why is winter driving more hazardous than other seasons?
options: a:There are increased hours of darkness.,b:Road conditions can be affected by freezing temperatures, ice, snow, and fog.,c:Both of the above.
note: Winter driving is more dangerous because there are more hours of darkness and road surfaces can become slippery or obscured by ice, snow, and fog. These conditions reduce traction and visibility, requiring slower speeds and greater following distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What general attitude should a driver have about right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
note: Right-of-way laws say who should go first, but they do not guarantee that others will follow them. Safe drivers always stay ready to yield, even when they legally have the right-of-way, if yielding will prevent a collision.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You should slow down, scan carefully for children, and be prepared to stop if they are in or near the crosswalk. You do not automatically stop unless required by a stop sign, signal, or pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: If a tire blows out suddenly while you're driving, what steps should you take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and exit the traffic lane slowly.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly to stop quickly.,c:Brake hard and steer immediately to the right edge.,d:Turn on your hazards and speed up to reach the shoulder faster.
note: When a tire blows out, the car may pull to one side. Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down. Once it is under control and speed has dropped, steer gradually off the road and brake gently if needed. Sudden hard braking or sharp steering can cause loss of control.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:One,b:Two,c:Three
note: Alcohol begins to affect judgment and reaction time with the first drink. Even one drink can impair your ability to drive safely, so the safest choice is not to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

question: What is the only thing that can reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Once alcohol is in your system, only time allows your body to metabolize it and lower your BAC. Food, coffee, cold showers, or exercise may make you feel more awake but do not speed up the elimination of alcohol.

question: When ridden on public roadways, bicycles are legally classified as:
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Vehicles.,c:Hazards.,d:Motor vehicles.
note: Bicycles ridden on public roads are treated as vehicles. Cyclists must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules just like drivers of cars, including stopping at red lights and stop signs and riding in the same direction as traffic.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the lap belt.
note: If your vehicle has both a lap belt and a shoulder belt, you must wear both. The lap belt should be low and snug across the hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the chest and shoulder, not the neck or under the arm. Using only one part greatly reduces protection in a crash.

question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: You must not make a U‑turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure it is safe. Limited visibility makes it hard to judge oncoming traffic and can lead to serious head‑on collisions.

question: Driving noticeably slower than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.,b:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,c:A good idea if the weather is bad, but you must not drive so slowly that you unnecessarily block or endanger other traffic.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because other drivers may not expect it and may make sudden or risky lane changes or passing maneuvers. You should generally travel at the speed of traffic (within the speed limit) and adjust your speed reasonably for conditions, such as bad weather, without becoming an unnecessary obstruction.

question: What qualifies as a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from the driving task—your eyes from the road, your mind from driving, or your hands from the wheel. Examples include texting, eating, adjusting controls, or focusing on passengers instead of traffic.

question: When following another vehicle at night, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
note: Use low beam headlights when following another vehicle at night so you do not shine bright light into the driver’s mirrors and eyes. High beams can blind or distract the driver ahead, increasing the risk of a crash.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Neither lane may pass.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe.
